metadata.Assessments: Chemisch Rekenen 1 - Written, organised by STAD examinations Histologie - Other assessment

/en/course/2026/BOVP23MDWEEFSELS.outcomes:
You explain the concepts of polarity and mol and apply them in simple chemical calculations, enabling you to apply basic chemistry and chemical arithmetic/mathematics knowledge to general laboratory skills.
You name the different parts of a microscope and explain their function, and you build up routine in microscopy by using the main microscopic techniques to study tissues. In the process, you delve into the functioning of different types of tissues.
You know and recognise the structure and appearance of the four tissue types (epithelium, muscle, connective and nerve) and colour a tissue section and give the correct designation(s) of the tissue as the basis of histology.
You name and describe the anatomy and physiology of the skin and musculoskeletal system and delve into various pathological conditions.
You will make overview and detail drawings of histological preparations of various tissues and organs according to drawing rules and display them in an ordered portfolio to correctly process microscopic images.

/en/course/2026/BOVP23MDWEEFSELS.content:
During this module, you will study the structure of different animal tissues based on theory and histological preparations on the practical course. During the lectures, you will complete in-depth assignments on the various tissues, the skin and the locomotor system.
In addition, during histology tutorials, under the supervision of a lecturer, you work out the practicals in a portfolio and have your work assessed and interpreted by a fellow student.
In this module, you also work with chemical calculations. You will practise the calculations during working lectures, followed by practice games of chemical calculation in teams.
Basic maths skills will also be covered in a working lecture during this module, which will also involve practice. At the end of the quarter, chemical arithmetic and basic mathematics will be tested individually in writing.

metadata.Assessments: Analytische Vaardigheden - Other assessment Metabolisme - Computer, organised by STAD examinations

/en/course/2026/BOVP23MDSPIJSVRT.outcomes:
You will name and describe the anatomy and physiology of the digestive system and understand the functioning of the metabolism of the biomolecules proteins, fats and carbohydrates as the basis of biochemistry and demonstrate this through a presentation including a photo/movie of a self-assembled biomolecule and its metabolism.
You delve further into the skills of a medical analyst by working with general laboratory skills (pipetting, weighing, use of glassware) to determine the influence of pH on digestion, applying basic chemical arithmetic and mathematics, including fractions, powers and logarithms.
You work safely in the laboratory by preparing a practical according to the applicable guidelines and correctly logging and processing results in the lab journal according to the logbook instruction for research skills.
You reflect on your study choice.

/en/course/2026/BOVP23MDSPIJSVRT.content:
In this module, you will study the metabolism of the three biomolecules – fats, proteins and carbohydrates – using the human digestive system as a model. Through a range of assignments, you will learn about the anatomy, physiology and histology of the digestive system and examine the chemical aspects of the metabolism of these biomolecules in detail. In the laboratory, you will learn basic skills such as selecting the correct glassware, weighing accurately, pipetting and recording your practical work in the logbook.
To conclude, you will sit a digital test on the metabolism of nutrients in the human body. You will incorporate all assignments into your anatomy portfolio.
You will complete the laboratory skills module with a practical test on pipetting and recording. Using the ‘start thermometer’, you will reflect on your choice of study programme and discuss this with your mentor.

metadata.Assessments: Microbiologie incl. VMT Certificering - Other assessment Wiskunde - Written, organised by STAD examinations

/en/course/2026/BOVP23MDMICROBM.outcomes:
Using clear instruction and your own work plan, you work safely in the laboratory according to VMT rules to learn aseptic work and cultivate and recognise microorganisms, and report experiments in the lab journal according to the applicable guidelines.
You give and receive peer feedback on the lab journal from a fellow student.
You correctly apply the arithmetic rules for solving second-degree equations, linear equations, equations with roots, power functions and logarithms, for describing formulas and for differentiating functions on obtained data during the practical.
You read an English-language article on the microbiome according to the instructions provided and present this article in a structured way to fellow students to delve into the basics of microbiology.

/en/course/2026/BOVP23MDMICROBM.content:
During the module ‘microbiome’ you perform the Safe Microbiological Techniques practical (3 practical days) and the E. coli practical (1 practical day). You conclude both practicals with a logbook. You discuss the VMT logs for feedback that you take into account in the concluding E. coli log.
You practise with a dataset for differentiation and create a growth curve based on the E. coli practical. Your mathematical skills are tested by means of a written test.
You and a group (3-4 students) read an English-language article that you read according to the instructions provided. You present this article to your fellow students. You give your fellow students feedback on their presentation.

metadata.Assessments: Urologische Diagnostiek en Statistiek - Other assessment

/en/course/2026/BOVP23MDURINEWEG.outcomes:
You will identify, describe and visualise the anatomy, histology and physiology of the urinary tract by analysing a patient case using self-assessment tests and clinical chemistry methods for determining creatinine and protein levels in urine samples.
You will apply basic statistical skills, including the normal distribution and confidence intervals, to datasets relating to creatinine and protein measurements, and visualise the results using Excel in order to assess data quality in terms of variability and reproducibility.
You will carry out the creatinine and protein measurements correctly in accordance with the guidelines, applying the theory of redox reactions; you will understand the principles of spectrophotometry and the resulting calculations, and explain these during a laboratory session.
You plan and evaluate your own study work and adjust your learning accordingly, thereby taking ownership of your learning process; you reflect in a reflection report on collaborating with fellow students and the importance of effective study methods.

/en/course/2026/BOVP23MDURINEWEG.content:
In this module, you will study the anatomy, physiology and histology of a healthy and a diseased kidney using patient case studies. You will do this by dissecting a kidney (macroscopic level) and by staining and examining histological sections (microscopic level). In addition, you will find an image of a histological section from a kidney patient, so that you can identify the differences at the histological level. You will compile the results of the associated assignments in your anatomy portfolio.
You will then take on the role of a medical analyst and study the effect of kidney damage in these patients in the laboratory by carrying out protein and creatinine assays. You will learn to relate the results of the experiments to the extent of kidney damage in a patient. Using Excel, you will learn to structure and visualise the data you generate. To interpret the structured data, you will apply basic statistical skills to a dataset. To conclude, you will individually demonstrate that you can create a correlated calibration curve and that you can visualise and structure a dataset and apply statistical tests to it. At the start of the module, you will evaluate your study habits and consciously adjust them throughout the module. At the end of this module, you will reflect on your study habits and your collaboration with fellow students over the past term.

metadata.Assessments: Chemical Calculations 2 - Written, organised by STAD examinations Gas exchange, pH, and Buffers - Other assessment

/en/course/2026/BOVP23MDADEM.outcomes:
You name and describe the anatomy and physiology of respiration and gas exchange, and examine and experience this during a cycling experiment, applying the theory of redox reactions to gas exchange and oxidative phosphorylation in cells.
You recognize and name the role of weak acids and bases in buffer systems, and you apply the chemical principles of acids, bases and buffers in physiological and in laboratory situations.
You apply chemical calculations with logarithms and logarithmic equations in the Henderson-Hasselbalch equation to correctly create buffers in the laboratory.
You will devise and conduct your own research project with a group of fellow students on a topic of your own choosing, formulating an appropriate research question, preparing a work plan, and executing this work plan to produce reliable and relevant results.

/en/course/2026/BOVP23MDADEM.content:
This module focuses on breathing. You will learn about the anatomy of airways and the importance of oxygen in energy metabolism. Gas exchange is necessary because oxygen is required in energy metabolism, which produces CO2. During a cycling test, you will measure for yourself what happens to respiration and gas exchange during exercise.
Respiration also involves blood pH regulation. You learn about the functions of buffers in the body. You calculate and investigate the function of buffers, focusing on the logarithmic pH scale. You learn what buffers are and make the buffers you will need in module 1.3.2.
You also make a start with an individual report and your own project. During modules 1.3.1, 1.3.2 and 1.3.3, you set up your own project, carry it out and present it with a poster.

metadata.Name: Immune System
metadata.Assessments: Biochemische Technieken - Other assessment Immunologie - Computer, organised by STAD examinations

/en/course/2026/BOVP23MDIMMUUN.outcomes:
You recognise and name the different components and functions of both the innate and acquired immune system.
You visualise and present in groups the different types of blood cells and their function in the human immune system as the basis of immunology.
You know and recognise the morphology and function of the different white blood cells and correctly prepare and differentiate (dift) a blood smear according to the basic rules of haematology.
You perform basic biochemical techniques SDS-PAGE and Western Blot to determine a specific protein in the blood and can explain the results obtained from both experiments.
You and a group of fellow students process the results of the research project carried out in module 1.3.1 according to the applicable guidelines for data processing and data visualisation.

/en/course/2026/BOVP23MDIMMUUN.content:
This module introduces you to the immune system and the main cells and proteins (such as antibodies) that play a role in it. The immune system is important in your body, but you also use parts of the immune system in some important experiments in the lab. For example, you use antibodies to detect a protein in a Western blot. Therefore, you will not only learn about the immune system in the body, but also how to use immunology in biochemical techniques.
You will also continue with the research project and individual report from module 1.3.1. During this module, you will have a working lecture on data processing and data visualisation. During the tutorial, you will work with your own data to process and display it properly. The product is a poster that you will present in module 1.3.3.

metadata.Name: Hormones
metadata.Assessments: Basisberoepscompetenties - Other assessment Endocrinologie - Computer, organised by STAD examinations

/en/course/2026/BOVP23MDHORMONEN.outcomes:
You identify and describe the anatomy and physiology of the endocrine system and a number of important (reproductive) hormones in the human body.
You will apply general knowledge of the principles of the basic chemical technique of chromatography in developing a method for the determination of a hormone using HPLC.
You will identify and describe the principles of a clinical chemistry assay, which you will carry out individually during the practical session, and you will analyse the experimental data by applying the appropriate statistical methods.
You analyse a health issue based on a patient case study and use general knowledge of immunological and basic chemical techniques to interpret data in order to determine the clinical picture; you then describe these results and conclusions individually in a case report.
Together with a group of fellow students, you will visualise and present the findings of the research project from module 1.3.1 in the form of a poster, accompanied by a poster presentation and pitch.

/en/course/2026/BOVP23MDHORMONEN.content:
The endocrine system consists of the organs that produce hormones. Hormones are signalling substances in the body. In this module, you will learn which organs form part of the endocrine system and what the hormones produced there do. At the end of the module, you will take a digital test on the endocrine system and hormones.
To understand how hormones are measured and what this means, you will be given a case study. You will be provided with various results from clinical chemistry tests to help you resolve your case study. You will analyse these results to determine which clinical picture corresponds to the case study. You will record your findings in an individual case report. In addition, during the practical session, you will individually carry out a clinical chemistry test, which will be assessed as a basic professional competence (BBC).
In this module, you will also complete the research project from modules 1.3.1 and 1.3.2 by presenting a poster on the project you have undertaken.

metadata.Name: Blood
metadata.Assessments: Analyse van Bloedwaarden - Other assessment Hart, Bloedvaten en Bloed - Computer, organised by STAD examinations

/en/course/2026/BOVP23MDBLOED.outcomes:
You name and describe the structure and function of bone tissue and the heart and blood vessels and explore cardiovascular systems while dissecting them to learn the anatomy and physiology of the heart, blood vessels and circulation in humans.
You will master the principles of determinations of various blood values, including blood coagulation, haemoglobin, haematocrit and blood groups, perform these determinations according to your own work plan and the general clinical chemical standards as the basis of haematology.
You and other students create a diagnostic case on aspirin coupled with an acid-base titration to determine the amount of aspirin and apply statistics to solve the case as an example of a drug determination in the laboratory and its clinical relevance.
You apply basic statistical skills by comparing laboratory results using difference tests, assessing their reliability and visualising these results in graphs in a correct, clear and unambiguous way, analysing the results.
You describe the physiological and chemical functions of buffers in blood and explain the balance and disturbances in this balance in physiological situations.
You handle patient material and patient data consciously and make ethical considerations according to appropriate guidelines on their use.

/en/course/2026/BOVP23MDBLOED.content: This module focuses on bone tissue and blood. In medical diagnostics, many parameters are measured in blood. You examine the composition and properties of blood. You dissect the heart and blood vessels and learn their anatomy and physiology and how blood cells are created in the bone marrow. You learn about the formation and breakdown of bone tissue. You differentiate different cell types in blood and determine, among other things, the haematocrit value and haemoglobin concentration and, as part of statistics, apply difference tests to laboratory results. Because you will be working with blood, you will also learn to work with biological material and the ethical aspects associated with it.

metadata.Name: Heredity
metadata.Assessments: Genetica en Erfelijkheid - Computer, organised by STAD examinations Moleculaire Technieken - Other assessment

/en/course/2026/BOVP23MDERFELIJK.outcomes:
You name, in the context of reproduction, the anatomy and physiology of the sexual organs, describe the menstrual cycle, illustrate the different phases of mitosis and meiosis and explain what takes place in the first stages after fertilisation.
You understand Mendelian inheritance, apply simple statistical tests to the inheritance of genetic traits and reason out the consequences of mutations in hereditary material as the basis of genetics.
You delve into an ethical aspect about reproduction, genetics or embryology and conduct a forum discussion on this with a group.
You master the principles of molecular biological techniques such as PCR, electrophoresis and restriction analysis, and together with a fellow student you make a work plan and digital prediction for the determination of a genetic trait, and correctly test this work plan against practice.
You reflect on the choice for this study by briefly summarising the guest lectures of last year and writing a report for your personal portfolio.

/en/course/2026/BOVP23MDERFELIJK.content: During this module, you will delve into the anatomy and physiology of the sex organs, learn about mitosis and meiosis and what happens in the first stages after fertilisation. You will work with molecular biological techniques in the context of reproduction and heredity and isolate your own DNA. You will also determine a hereditary trait (bitter tests) of yourself using PCR. You draw up a work plan in which you first simulate the mutation using bioinformatics assignments and then determine in the laboratory whether the mutation is present. With your fellow students, you discuss ethical aspects of reproduction and genetics. At the end of this module, you reflect on the past year, your choice of study and the coming academic year.

/en/course/2026/BOVH24MDPRMICRO.outcomes:
You analyse, assess and identify micro-organisms in microbiological samples using selective media, biochemical and molecular techniques, and various staining methods as part of your microbiological laboratory skills.
You will carry out antibiotic susceptibility tests and interpret the results to determine the antibiotic resistance profiles of microorganisms representative of clinical samples.
You will isolate bacterial and viral DNA/RNA from various sources, detecting specific viruses and bacteria using various PCR techniques as an example of virus and bacterial detection within medical microbiology.
You will gain an understanding of the objectives of the Year 2 mentoring programme for the Medical Diagnostics course through an introductory session with your mentor. You will also meet your mentor during a one-to-one meeting and submit a completed handover form (in advance).
/en/course/2026/BOVH24MDPRMICRO.content: During the practical sessions, you will work on identifying micro-organisms in clinical samples using various tests. You will culture micro-organisms on selective media and carry out various biochemical tests and staining procedures. You will also determine the antibiotic susceptibility of the isolated micro-organisms. You will compile the results in a written report. In addition, you will isolate and examine the presence of bacterial and viral genetic material from various sources, and learn to apply various PCR techniques for detection.

metadata.Name: Medical Microbiology
metadata.Assessments: Microbiologie 1 - Computer, organised by STAD examinations Microbiologie 2 - Computer, organised by STAD examinations

/en/course/2026/BOVH24MDMEDMICRO.outcomes:
You identify and describe the structure and function of (parts of) prokaryotic cells and establish links between the structure and physiology of the microorganism – including metabolism and biosynthesis – both from a general cell biology perspective and as applied in medical diagnostics, using the correct medical terminology.
You have an understanding of growth and the factors influencing that growth in various parts of a healthy body, and establish links with the physiological functions of microorganisms in these locations.
You are familiar with and understand the (virulence) factors that influence the growth, multiplication and spread of microorganisms in invasive pathological conditions, and relate the action of a number of antibiotics and antiviral agents to the molecular structure and metabolism of microorganisms and the development of resistance to them.
You analyse the patient’s medical history and clinical and microbiological laboratory results, and use these to explain the onset and progression of infectious diseases in the human body.
/en/course/2026/BOVH24MDMEDMICRO.content:
Microbiology 1 provides an introduction to the field of microbiology. Understanding the physiological characteristics and behaviour of microorganisms provides insight and knowledge needed in medical diagnostics for the detection, identification and treatment of infectious diseases.
Microbiology 2 focuses on (opportunistically) pathogenic bacteria and viruses. Various micro-organisms are discussed in detail, covering both the diseases they cause, diagnostics in the laboratory and the action of antimicrobial agents.

metadata.Name: Professional Competences 1
metadata.Assessments: Diagnostische Methoden - Computer, organised by STAD examinations Projectmanagement en Kwaliteitszorg - Other assessment

/en/course/2026/BOVH24MDBEROEP1.outcomes:
You understand the operation of a number of important general biochemical and molecular diagnostic methods and relate the function and properties of biomolecules (e.g. enzymes, antibodies, probes) to these methods.
You understand the principles and applications of a number of physicochemical separation techniques (e.g. electrophoresis, centrifugation, HPLC, GC) and detection methods (mass) spectrometry, fluorescence) within medical diagnostics.
You will understand the principles and applications of some key molecular diagnostic techniques in medical diagnostics.
Together with fellow students, you delve into a diagnostic method by means of a literature study and you present the results in a relevant way to an audience of your peers, being aware of your role in the group process and the importance of your didactics for the understanding of this method.
In preparation for running a laboratory independently, you show awareness of your role in a group process, and of the importance of quality assurance in generating and delivering reliable results.
/en/course/2026/BOVH24MDBEROEP1.content:
In Diagnostic Methods, the first few weeks of short lectures will give you an overview of important physico-chemical separation techniques and molecular biological methods that are important for medical diagnostics. This is followed by assignments to further develop your knowledge. After this foundation, you and your fellow students will explore specific techniques and their application in the diagnostics of infectious organisms and hereditary diseases.
During the meetings, you will work together on the development and presentation of your diagnostic method, with lecturers present for theoretical support. These contact moments are used to work on understanding, analysing and interpreting issues in the context of (in-depth) assignments around diagnostic methods. Finally, you present the diagnostic method in class.
At the same time, in this module you will learn the relevance of both to an (optimally functioning) laboratory through the assignments project management and quality assurance.

/en/course/2026/BOVH24MDPRLABGEN.outcomes:
You will set up a clinical chemistry laboratory as part of a team, including establishing a LIMS system, division of tasks and roles, call protocol and SOPs to receive, record, process, analyze and report patient samples, taking into account (data) safety, privacy, efficiency, reliability and reproducibility of results.
You will perform a variety of key clinical chemistry analytical methods, such as ELISA, HPLC and enzyme kinetics assay, applying a structured experimental approach in each case to achieve reliable analysis of results, and elaborate these results in a logbook and measurement letters.
You analyze blood components by manual and automated diffen, compare both these methods in a validation report, and diagnose both white and red blood cell abnormalities by describing and analyzing unknown (abnormal) blood images.
/en/course/2026/BOVH24MDPRLABGEN.content:
During the labs, you work partly on “regular” labs to learn important molecular biological and chemical techniques associated with clinical chemistry and hematology. At the same time, you also prepare as a team for the shop floor simulation that takes place later in the year. Here you will learn more about the logistics and working methods in laboratory medicine and get acquainted with the handling of patient data and patient material taking into account the ethical aspects involved such as safety and privacy. You will also learn important aspects of quality assurance and the application of quality controls.
You will also create in this module some typical professional products from Medical Diagnostics, such as an SOP and a validation report.

metadata.Name: Laboratory Medicine
metadata.Assessments: Klinische Chemie en Hematologie 1 - Computer, organised by STAD examinations Klinische Chemie en Hematologie 2 - Computer, organised by STAD examinations

/en/course/2026/BOVH24MDLABGEN.outcomes:
You name and describe concrete actions and determinations in a clinical laboratory and relate these to the more general context, processes and logistics of a clinical (analytical) laboratory.
You apply aspects of quality assurance and validation (including sensitivity and specificity) to clinical chemical and hematological diagnostic tests according to the standards of good laboratory practice, you make calculations relevant to this, and you understand the importance of quality assurance and controls in the daily practice of laboratory medicine.
You understand anatomy, physiology and pathology in the areas of water, electrolyte and pH balance, hormones, glucose balance, kidney, heart and liver in the human body and know the most common diagnostic determinations.
You understand the anatomy, physiology and pathology regarding blood components, such as red blood cells, platelets, growth factors and blood clotting in the human body and know the most common diagnostic determinations.
You analyze patient cases using the knowledge gained and relate the given context and underlying mechanisms to arrive at interpretation and interpretation of clinical data from the clinical question to the diagnosis and treatment of the patient.
/en/course/2026/BOVH24MDLABGEN.content:
Laboratory medicine includes the disciplines of hematology and clinical chemistry. In clinical chemistry and hematology 1, you will learn about the logistics of clinical chemistry laboratories and the importance of quality assurance in general. In addition, for some of the most commonly requested determinations, you will learn the associated knowledge of anatomy, physiology, pathology and the process and operation of diagnostic determinations.
In clinical chemistry and hematology 2, you will learn to integrate and apply the knowledge with case histories. Here you learn to interpret relevant data from the history and known laboratory results using the knowledge offered, and to combine knowledge of different (organ) systems in the body. This is a way of thinking that requires some practice.
Therefore, in this module we have chosen to do part of the knowledge transfer independently in the form of self-study with flash lectures and teaching materials at home, and in the contact moments instead to work on understanding, analyzing and interpreting issues in the context of (in-depth) assignments and case histories. With the help of self-checks you can check how much you have already understood prior to the lesson. This will be explained in the first lecture.
Simultaneously with this module you will learn how a clinical laboratory functions in practice and you will learn to perform a number of clinical chemical and hematological determinations.

metadata.Name: Professional Competences 2
metadata.Assessments: Data: Statistiek en Viisualisatie - Other assessment Laboratoriumcompetenties - Written, organised by STAD examinations

/en/course/2026/BOVH24MDBEROEP2.outcomes:
You will make an appropriate choice of an analytical method for a given experimental design, apply this method and present the results in an orderly fashion using appropriate software, including Excel and SPSS.
You perform various uni- and multivariate linear and nonlinear regression methods, including model selection, and you engage in interpolation with reliability and detection limit (for calibration) and extrapolation with reliability (for standard addition) and interpret these results for a given data set.
You understand and perform validation of measurement methods for continuous and nominal measurement values in order to advise on the method used.
You perform correct and insightful calculations in the context of the laboratory, extracting from a more complex context the correct data and question to arrive at this calculation.
/en/course/2026/BOVH24MDBEROEP2.content:
The 'Data: statistics and visualization' section introduces you to regression analysis and explores the comparison of different measurement methods and how to statistically process the results. You will use both Excel and SPSS, practicing on assignments. You will also practice with clearly visualizing and organizing your data. At the end you make a final assignment individually and hand it in.
For the section 'Laboratory Competencies' you look back at the theory on mathematics and chemical calculation from year 1 and the lab experiences you have gained so far in the field of preparation and elaboration of practicals and the associated calculations. On the basis of these experiences we deepen your theoretical knowledge and calculation skills a little more, so that you are well equipped to prepare and carry out calculations in more complex experiments in year 2 and year 3. This part will be tested individually in writing by means of an examination with applied calculation problems such as you can expect in the laboratory in year 2 and 3.

/en/course/2026/BOVH24MDPRGEN.outcomes:
You understand and independently perform several important molecular techniques within the genetic field, including FISH and (real-time) PCR as a basis of general laboratory skills within genetics.
You independently prepare a plan to develop, perform and optimize a PCR using bioinformatics tools.
You analyze and interpret the results of different molecular techniques and report them in a logbook according to the applicable guidelines.
You independently process the results of a genetic study in a report according to the applicable reporting guidelines, placing the results in the broader medical context and describing the relevance for medical diagnostics.
/en/course/2026/BOVH24MDPRGEN.content: This theme focuses on common diagnostics within the field of medical genetics. During the practical days, you will perform various molecular techniques, including RNA isolation, quantitative real-time PCR and fluorescent in situ hybridization (FISH). Among other things, you will set up your own PCR, optimize it by developing primers, and detect chromosomal abnormalities with FISH and real-time PCR.

metadata.Name: Medical Genetics
metadata.Assessments: Bio-Informatica - Other assessment Medische Genetica - Computer, organised by STAD examinations

/en/course/2026/BOVH24MDMEDGEN.outcomes:
You explain and draw how mitotic and meiotic division proceeds in human cells and reason about the consequences of nondisjunction of chromosomes during this division as the basis of medical genetics.
You will explain the various forms of aneuploidy (chromosomal abnormalities) and chromosome mutations and reason how they are inherited in humans giving examples of disorders that may result.
You understand epigenetic concepts and genomic imprinting and apply these concepts to explain why they may affect the development of inherited disorders.
You explain and apply the concepts of allele frequency and population genetics in medical genetics issues, relating them to factors that influence them and using calculations to predict how often these disorders occur in a population.
You work out a case, in which you analyze a genealogical pedigree for the purpose of (pre-)diagnostic research of hereditary diseases, analyze and interpret the results of a number of molecular biological techniques used in medical genetics using basic bioinformatics as part of working out a case.
/en/course/2026/BOVH24MDMEDGEN.content:
Medical genetics is a specialty within medicine that deals with the diagnosis and manageability of inherited disorders. With current developments in human genetics, more and more hereditary diseases can be detected. Within this module, you will learn how inherited disorders arise and how to detect them.
You will begin with a brief review of mitosis and meiosis and learn how they arise and what consequences they have. Then you will look at mutations and chromosomal abnormalities and how they arise. A number of examples will be covered, where you will find out how they can be inherited.
You will also learn about different techniques, such as (next generation) sequencing and karyotyping, used in diagnostics. You will analyze results from these techniques using bioinformatics, covering both the techniques and the analysis in silico. You will use the results to independently solve a case.

metadata.Name: Professional Competences 3
metadata.Assessments: Internationalisering - Other assessment Werkvloersimulatie - Other assessment

/en/course/2026/BOVH24MDBEROEP3.outcomes:
You know different aspects of intercultural communication and intercultural cooperation and reflect during working lectures, (online) group meetings and in an individual reflection report on these aspects and your intercultural communication and cooperation.
You carry out a research project as a group in an international project group where you present the findings orally in English to all participants.
You contribute to the international project week by participating with an open mind and respect in the social and cultural activities and fulfilling a task within it.
You run a clinical chemistry laboratory as a team: you receive biological samples , record and analyze them by performing various determinations - using the (self-developed) SOPs and preparations from previous modules -, coordinate logistics, handle biological material and patient data safely and reliably, and communicate correctly with team members, physician, clinical chemist and patients.
You work effectively together as a team where you are able to agree on division of labor and communication and act appropriately on unexpected events during the shop floor simulation.
/en/course/2026/BOVH24MDBEROEP3.content:
Project 1:
During International Project Week, intercultural and international cooperation is the focus. By, among other things, setting up and conducting a research project as an international project group, these aspects will be addressed during the collaboration. To achieve this, there will be a physical exchange with several partner colleges in Europe. There will also be an active focus on the various aspects of intercultural communication and cooperation in working lectures and (online)groupmeetings.
Project 2:
The work floor simulation focuses on setting up and running a “proper” laboratory. Students are guided with guided assignments and in meetings towards being able to successfully run the lab.

metadata.Name: Practical Histology and Cytology
metadata.Assessments: Praktijk Histologie en Cytologie - Other assessment

/en/course/2026/BOVH24MDPRHISCYT.outcomes:
You will make a representative cervical preparation using the cytospin, implement changes in the protocol of PAP staining and discuss the effect of these changes on the results compared to the standard procedure, thus gaining insight into important steps in the staining process and techniques in cervical cytology.
You will cut sections of paraffin blocks with a microtome and determine the origin of tumor tissue using histochemical and immunological staining as an important basis for the field of cytology and pathology.
You will work out results from the flow cytometer and May-Grünwald Giemsa staining of various B and T cell experiments and relate the results to each other.
/en/course/2026/BOVH24MDPRHISCYT.content: In this module you will learn important techniques from the field of histopathology and cytology. In this field, it is important to practice a lot with making, viewing and evaluating specimens and tissues. Here you will look in specimens to see if tumor cells are present. You will also learn the importance and significance of various histochemical and immunological stains

metadata.Name: Pathology
metadata.Assessments: Medical Immunology - Computer, organised by STAD examinations Pathology and Cytology - Computer, organised by STAD examinations

/en/course/2026/BOVH24MDPATH.outcomes:
You explain in detail how and where the cells and proteins of the innate and adaptive immune systems are formed and activated; you describe their role in fighting infection; and you explain how changes in the immune system lead to disease.
You apply your knowledge of the principles of the main immunological methods to solve simple diagnostic problems and make suggestions for appropriate diagnostic procedures in cases of immune system disorders.
You explain in detail reversible and irreversible cell damage and forms of cell death, and you apply this knowledge to a clinical case by analysing and presenting the causes, mechanisms and symptoms of pathological processes to fellow students.
You will explain the aetiology, diagnosis, biological mechanisms and epidemiology of tumours, and you will use this knowledge to analyse and present practice-oriented issues and case studies.
You will understand how the immune system works, describe inflammatory responses, and apply this knowledge to recognising and explaining immunopathological disorders (including autoimmune diseases, allergies and immunodeficiencies) using relevant case studies.
You can recognise and distinguish between normal and reactive benign cervical cells and neoplastic squamous cells in cytological smears of the cervical region on the basis of morphological characteristics.
/en/course/2026/BOVH24MDPATH.content:
In this module, you will learn the basics of cytology and pathology, and we will explore medical immunology in greater depth. In Medical Immunology, you will study the development and functioning of the innate and adaptive immune systems. Special attention is also given to the inflammatory response, the complement system, the MHC system, various immunological laboratory techniques and how disturbances in the immune system can lead to disease. This sub-module consists of theory lectures and seminars.
In Pathology and Cytology, the emphasis is on pathology, with a focus on the diseased cell, and you will learn to recognise healthy and pathological cells and tissues. You will explore the mechanisms of reversible and irreversible cell damage and cell death, and apply this knowledge to pathological conditions. During the lectures, you will learn about various aspects of tumours, such as different diagnostic methods, key underlying molecular processes and possible causes leading to tumour growth and metastasis, and you will gain knowledge of tumour epidemiology. Finally, you will explore various immune-related pathologies, such as hypersensitivity reactions, autoimmunity, immunodeficiency and transplant reactions, by understanding and applying the underlying mechanisms and their consequences. In addition, you will work in groups on a case study based on the course material and present this to the class.
A special component of the course is cervical pathology, in which you will study the cytology of the cervical mucosa. You will learn to recognise normal cervical cell patterns, identify various non-neoplastic and iatrogenic cellular changes, and study the precancerous stages of cervical squamous cell carcinoma. In this way, you will understand the pathogenesis of cervical carcinoma in relation to the morphological changes in the epithelium.

metadata.Name: Project 1
metadata.Assessments: Project work 1 - Other assessment Projectmanagement - Other assessment

/en/course/2026/BOVH26MDPROJECT1.outcomes:
This module has the following learning outcomes:
You will draw up and carry out a research plan, both independently and as part of a team, and apply a research strategy whilst taking into account the specific safety, environmental, hygiene and health and safety aspects.
You will analyse, interpret and evaluate research results obtained independently, and report and present the results through, amongst other things, progress meetings, presentations and a written professional assignment.
You will apply project management skills throughout the project and demonstrate this by independently formulating and defining project objectives.
You will set learning objectives to meet the competencies of this module and discuss these with your mentor.
/en/course/2026/BOVH26MDPROJECT1.content:
In this module, you will carry out a practice-oriented project in which you apply medical diagnostic techniques within a realistic professional setting. You will carry out a project at Hanze University, for example as part of one of the KCBBE’s research projects, or you will visit an external diagnostic laboratory, such as the UMCG or Certe. You will work on a medical biology research project, in which you will design, carry out and account for your research both independently and as part of a team. You will apply various laboratory techniques, work with professional equipment and carry out the analyses in accordance with applicable quality, safety and environmental standards.
You will learn to draw up a work plan, translate research questions into measurable tests, and critically analyse research results, underpinning them with relevant theory.
During the project, you will develop your research skills, learn to handle data and results with care, and become familiar with the specific working methods, responsibilities and professional ethics within the field of medical diagnostics.
The focus is also on project management, for which you will undertake a number of assignments, learning to work with others in a structured and systematic way to resolve a question or problem. You will formulate the project objective and design an approach for your research project, incorporating and describing suitable methods and techniques.

metadata.Name: Oncology and Pathology
metadata.Assessments: Portfolio Oncology and Pathology - Other assessment Theory Oncology and Pathology - Computer, organised by STAD examinations

/en/course/2026/BOVH26MDPATHONC.outcomes:
This module has the following learning outcomes:
You will describe the cell cycle and its regulation in eukaryotes, and predict the consequences of changes in (the regulation of) the cell cycle for the cell, the tissue and the organism as a whole.
You will recognise different types of DNA alterations, identify their possible causes and speculate on their potential effects at the protein and cellular levels.
You will study the pathology of tumour tissue in depth; you will be familiar with various biological markers and be able to apply them to determine the presence of tumour cells; and you will understand the operation and function of various (radiological) techniques.
You apply your knowledge of the anatomy and physiology of the cardiovascular and respiratory systems, the kidneys, the liver, the gut and the endocrine pancreas to explain the health effects that occur in the pathology of these (organ) systems.
You use your biological knowledge to explain different forms of cancer and pathological conditions, and you speculate on potential targets for treatment.
You explore a topic relevant to oncology and pathology in depth and present both in a relevant manner to an audience of your peers.
/en/course/2026/BOVH26MDPATHONC.content:
This module covers various aspects of oncology and pathology, building on the Pathology and Cytology module from Year 2. It briefly covers the causes, pathology, analytical techniques used and possible treatments for tumours. Furthermore, this module also discusses (examples of) the pathology of various organ systems. Using various medical case studies (‘patients’), the anatomy and (dys)function of the cardiovascular system, the respiratory system, the liver, the kidneys and the endocrine pancreas are covered.
This module comprises lectures and seminars. During these sessions, you will work through the theory yourself, which will be assessed individually. In addition, each student, working in pairs, will deliver a short theoretical lecture on an oncological topic relevant to this module. You will also work on a case study (a pathological condition) in pairs to apply the theory directly. This module ties in with the topics of the Year 3 projects, in which the theory covered in this module can be used to understand the biological background of the projects.

metadata.Name: Project 2
metadata.Modes of delivery: Assignment Guest lecture Lecture Project-based learning Teaching method 1 Tutorial
metadata.Assessments: Organisation and Management - Other assessment Project Work 2 - Other assessment

/en/course/2026/BOVH26MDPROJECT2.outcomes:
This module has the following learning outcomes:
You will draw up and carry out a research plan, both independently and as part of a team, and apply a research strategy whilst taking into account the specific safety, environmental, hygiene and health and safety aspects.
You analyse, interpret and evaluate research results you have obtained yourself, and report and present the results through, amongst other things, progress meetings, presentations and a written professional assignment.
You proactively seek feedback from your supervisor on your performance in relation to each competence and, where necessary, identify areas for improvement to guide your own performance and development. You can use this for Project 3.
You describe how, during your studies, you have shared knowledge about the programme (for example, with prospective students) as part of your professional engagement.
You are aware of the competences you have developed by linking them to professional practice; you can recognise organisational structures and cultures and act appropriately in response; you demonstrate an understanding of the relevant professional field and the labour market; and you learn how to apply for jobs through job application training.
/en/course/2026/BOVH26MDPROJECT2.content:
In this module, you will carry out a practice-oriented project in which you apply medical diagnostic techniques within a realistic professional setting. You will carry out a project at Hanze University, for example as part of one of the KCBBE’s research projects, or you will visit an external diagnostic laboratory, such as the UMCG or Certe. You will work on a medical biology research project, in which you will design, carry out and account for your research both independently and as part of a team. You will apply various laboratory techniques, work with professional equipment and carry out the analyses in accordance with applicable quality, safety and environmental standards.
You will learn to draw up a work plan, translate research questions into measurable tests, and critically analyse research results, underpinning them with relevant theory.
During the project, you will develop your research skills, learn to handle data and results with care, and become familiar with the specific working methods, responsibilities and professional ethics within the field of medical diagnostics.
Organisation and Management aims to raise your awareness of the professional field. It does this by teaching you to bridge the gap between the competences acquired during the programme and real-world practice in the workplace. For example: by taking another close look at the competences (knowledge, skills, attitude). But also by providing insight into organisational structures and cultures (how do you adapt within an organisation?). Through labour market orientation (exploring the market and guest speakers from the field) and through job application training, you will start to focus on your career.

metadata.Name: Hematology en Clinical Immunology
metadata.Assessments: Clinical Immunology - Computer, organised by STAD examinations Hematology - Computer, organised by STAD examinations

/en/course/2026/BOVH26MDHEMAKLIN.outcomes:
You explain in detail how the various white blood cells develop from stem cells, what functions the different cell types perform in the body, and what morphological and functional abnormalities are observed in patients.
You describe how a number of important chromosomal mutations (deletions, inversions, translocations) are involved in the development of acute and chronic leukaemias, which techniques and parameters are used for diagnosis, and what treatment options are available, including stem cell transplantation.
You explain which blood groups and screening procedures are important when preparing for and carrying out a blood transfusion, and apply this knowledge to real-world examples.
You explain the main characteristics, causes and mechanisms of autoimmune diseases, autoinflammatory diseases, and primary and secondary immunodeficiencies, and link this knowledge to the role of the immune system.
/en/course/2026/BOVH26MDHEMAKLIN.content:
In Haematology, the focus will be on the function and abnormalities of white blood cells. Considerable attention will be paid to the molecular aetiology, diagnosis, classification and subsequent treatment of leukaemias. The recently introduced CAR T-cell therapy will be presented in a guest lecture by the UMCG. In addition, the practical aspects of blood transfusion will be discussed, including transfusion testing during pregnancy and childbirth.
The Clinical Immunology submodule offers an in-depth overview of conditions in which the immune system plays a central role, through lectures, seminars and a guest lecture. It covers autoimmune diseases, in which the immune system attacks the body’s own tissues, and autoinflammatory diseases arising from an improperly regulated immune system. In addition, primary immunodeficiencies are covered: congenital abnormalities of the immune system and secondary immunodeficiencies, which arise due to external factors such as infections, medication or malignancies.

/en/course/2026/BOVH26MDSTAGE.outcomes:
The learning outcomes you are working towards are the programme-level learning outcomes. These can also be found on the Hanze website.
You will carry out practice-oriented research independently, translating a given problem into a research strategy and conducting the research, thereby contributing to the resolution of a current and/or socially relevant issue within the field of Applied Science.
Under supervision, you will design experiments, carry them out independently and systematically, and generate reproducible and reliable results that can be used to answer a practice-oriented research question within the Applied Science domain.
You operate within the framework of a management system, ensuring that your own work complies with applicable procedures and contributes to safeguarding quality, safety and compliance with legislation and regulations within an organisation in the Applied Science domain.
You gain a thorough understanding of the client’s problems and/or requirements and describe the context, enabling you to contribute to proposing a possible course of action within the field of Applied Science.
Upon request, you share your own knowledge and skills with others within the field of Applied Science, enabling them to gain a basic understanding of the use of relevant methods, equipment and tasks.
You work in a structured and systematic manner with others on a project within a limited, open project framework in the field of Applied Science.
/en/course/2026/BOVH26MDSTAGE.content:
To prepare you for professional practice, the programme includes a work placement. The aim of this work placement is to prepare you for the professional working environment. The focus of the work placement is on learning to function in the professional field by carrying out a work placement assignment. You will undertake your placement at a placement organisation, such as a company, hospital, university, research institute, etc. You will work under the supervision of a placement supervisor. The placement is worth 30 EC, during which you will work on developing your final-year competencies.
For information on graduation, the Brightspace course ‘Internship and Graduation’ is available. OnStage is used as the administration system.
The internship lasts 20 weeks. You will begin by drawing up a plan of action, carry out the work, and conclude the internship with a portfolio and a poster presentation. The portfolio comprises set and optional components, through which you demonstrate your competences. Halfway through the placement period, an interim evaluation will be scheduled with you, your placement supervisor and your contact lecturer.
During the placement period, review sessions will be organised to assist you with the placement process, the portfolio and the poster presentation.

/en/course/2026/BOVH26MDAFST.outcomes:
The learning outcomes you are working towards are the programme-level learning outcomes. These can also be found at www.mijnhanze.nl.
You will carry out practice-oriented research independently, translating a given problem into a research strategy and conducting the research, thereby contributing to the resolution of a current and/or socially relevant issue within the field of Applied Science.
Under supervision, you will set up experiments, carry them out independently and systematically, and generate reproducible and reliable results that can be used to answer a practice-oriented research question within the Applied Science domain.
You operate within the framework of a management system, ensuring that your own work complies with applicable procedures and contributes to safeguarding quality, safety and compliance with legislation and regulations within an organisation in the Applied Science domain.
You gain a thorough understanding of the client’s problems and/or requirements and describe the context, so that you can contribute to proposing a possible course of action within the field of Applied Science.
Upon request, you share your own knowledge and skills with others within the field of Applied Science, so that they gain a basic understanding of the use of relevant methods, equipment and tasks.
You work in a structured and systematic manner with others on a project within a limited, open project framework in the field of Applied Science.
/en/course/2026/BOVH26MDAFST.content:
You will carry out your final-year research project independently at a company, hospital, university or research institute. You will work under the supervision of a company supervisor. The final-year project is worth 30 EC, during which you will develop your final-year-level competencies.
For information about the final-year project, the Brightspace course ‘Work Placement and Final-Year Project’ is available. OnStage is used as the administration system.
The final-year project period lasts 20 weeks. You will begin by drafting a project plan, carry out the research and conclude the project with a portfolio and a defence. The portfolio comprises set and optional components, through which you will demonstrate your competences. Halfway through the graduation period, an interim evaluation is scheduled with you, your graduation supervisor and your contact lecturer.
The organisation where the final-year project is carried out must offer you the opportunity to work on a project that fits the programme profile of your course and through which you can demonstrate the competences required at the final level of your course.

/en/course/2026/CIVP26FOM.outcomes:
Learning Outcomes
LOL1: Setting the Direction
The Marketing Management (MM) professional identifies new opportunities for sustainable competitive advantage in national and international markets and, based on this analysis, determines the commercial direction of a product, service, brand, or organisation.
Level 1:
The beginning Marketing Management (MM) professional prepares simple short- or medium-term marketing plans for a product, service, brand, or organisation. The student applies basic marketing and organisational theory and uses insights from the internal and external environment of the organisation. The student explains the choices made and supports these with simple calculations of possible outcomes.
/en/course/2026/CIVP26FOM.content:
Content
This course introduces you to the field of marketing. It is based on the textbook Principles of Marketing by Kotler and focuses on the key concepts that form the foundation of the Marketing Management programme. You will learn how markets function, how customers think and behave, and how organisations create value through segmentation, targeting, positioning, and the marketing mix.
The course connects theory with practice by using real-life examples. These examples show how marketing decisions are made in dynamic and global environments. By the end of the course, you will understand core marketing concepts and how they are applied in practice.
These fundamental concepts will be revisited in later courses, where you will further develop, deepen, and apply them at a more advanced level.
Literature/study materials
See Brightspace or intranet.

/en/course/2026/CIVP26MES.content:
Content
This module combines a group project with a focused development of the skills needed to complete it successfully. You will work in groups on a real-life business case and conduct both primary research (data you collect yourself) and secondary research (existing data) to determine an appropriate marketing mix.
Alongside the project work, you will develop key skills in project management, academic writing, and presentation. Assessment is based on a written report, a group presentation, and additional required deliverables.

/en/course/2026/CIVP26PRD.content:
Content
In this course, you will develop a validated product or service based on an identified need or problem. You will also assess its economic viability. The course introduces you to the core principles of design thinking and provides insight into the financial aspects of a business plan.
Key topics include all stages of the design thinking process (empathy, definition, ideation, prototyping, testing, and implementation), as well as essential financial concepts such as break-even analysis, operating leverage, cost price calculation, and budget variance.
Throughout the course, you will be supported by learning activities that help you apply the theory in practice. Generative artificial intelligence (AI) tools are used to support learning and skill development. By the end of the course, you will understand how the design thinking process and financial analysis support effective business plan decision-making.

This course introduces the core principles of sales and provides insight into the economic aspects of marketing and sales decisions. You will study the role of the salesperson, the skills required for effective selling, and the key success factors that support sales performance.
Key topics include pricing and its impact on demand, market structures, the three Ps (people, planet, and profit), and different types of business cycles. Throughout the course, theory is supported by learning activities that help you apply the concepts in practice and understand how sales decisions influence organisational success.
By the end of the course, you will understand how to develop effective sales strategies, operate in real-life sales situations, and use microeconomic and macroeconomic factors to support informed decision-making.

/en/course/2026/CIVB25UCB.outcomes:
Learning Outcomes
After completing this course the student is able to:
Show understanding of how consumers learn and retain new product information and how the sense of self, needs, emotions, and motivations of consumers influence their purchases
Show understanding of how consumer attitudes are formed, how decision-making works, and how these processes can be influenced through various marketing stimuli or aspects of the shopping environment, both online and at physical stores
Select and apply different market research methods, qualitative and quantitative, to design appropriate research approaches to solve marketing issues related to consumer behaviour and evaluation of marketing stimuli
Analyse real-life consumption choices over a given period of time, critically evaluate them through the lens of applicable theory taught in the course, and reflect on what was learned from this analysis
/en/course/2026/CIVB25UCB.content:
Content
This course explores how and why people make buying decisions. You will learn how consumers perceive, process, and remember product information, and how factors such as emotions, needs, motivations, and sense of self influence their choices. The course also examines how consumer attitudes are formed and how decision-making processes work in practice.
You will study how organisations can influence consumer behaviour through marketing activities such as advertising and the design of physical stores and digital environments. Both online and in-person shopping experiences are addressed.
In addition, you will develop practical skills in market research. Both qualitative and quantitative research approaches are covered. This will help you understand how market research supports organisations in making informed marketing decisions.
You will analyse real-life buying decisions consumers make and apply relevant theories to understand these choices. You will also reflect on what these decisions reveal about consumer behaviour.
By the end of the course, you will be able to explain how consumers make decisions, assess how marketing influences these decisions, and apply research tools to study consumer behaviour effectively. These skills are relevant for careers in marketing, advertising, and business strategy.
Literature/study materials

This course equips students with the knowledge and skills to address marketing business problems using quantitative research methods. You will develop a deep understanding of statistical concepts and techniques and learn how to apply these tools to analyze and interpret data effectively.
Through hands-on experience with data analysis tools, you will learn to execute appropriate statistical tests, interpret data, and present findings in a clear, professional manner. The course emphasizes practical application, enabling you to make data-driven decisions in real business contexts.
