/en/course/2026/WBVP24IP.outcomes:
The early-career professional
1    collaborates effectively within a technical project, takes ownership of their own contribution, communicates clearly and respectfully, and, as part of a team, delivers an agreed project outcome, ensuring that the joint construction  and development process proceeds in a focused and responsible manner.
2    under supervision, investigates the operation of a simple thermal system by carrying out measurements, making observations and recognising the basic principles of heat transfer, so that conclusions can be drawn about the function, operation and energy behaviour of the system.
3    applies, under supervision, a simple design method to develop a functional component of a thermal system, and produces a workable design that meets the project brief.
4    constructs, under supervision, a simple component of a thermal system, carries out a basic test and reports findings, so that the component functions in accordance with the project agreements and contributes to the system as a whole.
/en/course/2026/WBVP24IP.content:
In this module, first-year mechanical engineering students are introduced to the entire process of developing a technical solution within the field of energy engineering. Students work in teams on a physical component of a thermal setup, learning in the process to collaborate on projects, communicate effectively and take responsibility. They investigate how a simple thermal system functions by measuring, observing and applying the basic principles of heat transfer and fluid mechanics.
Building on these insights, students design a simple, functional component. They then build and test this component, thereby actively linking theory and practice.
The module thus lays the foundation for professional competence, investigative skills, ownership and collaborative learning. Students experience how collaboration, research, design and fabrication are inextricably linked in the professional practice of a mechanical engineer, and how technical choices contribute to responsible, safe and sustainable working practices.

determines the most heavily loaded cross-section(s) and calculates the resulting theoretical stress, comparing it to the allowable stress
creates a calculation report where the calculations/modeling are linked to the real-life situation.
/en/course/2026/WBVP24MD1.content: In this module, the student is introduced to metals and their material properties. For simple situations, the student can isolate components and calculate the resulting theoretical stress for these components, verifying whether the stress is permissible. Additionally, the student learns how such calculations should be documented.

metadata.Name: Modelling & Manufacturing
metadata.Assessments: Manufacturing Engineering - Assignment SW Modelling - Assignment Workplace - Assignment

/en/course/2026/WBVP24MF.outcomes:
The student:
models components in 3D with fully defined sketches.
creates assemblies of multiple components with interrelated connections.
describes production methods and their corresponding applications.
learns to work with the production methods available in the workshop.
/en/course/2026/WBVP24MF.content: In this module, a student learns how various products are produced. Additionally, the student can convert these real-world products into a 3D model.

metadata.Name: Project Powered Device
metadata.Assessments: Professional Identity - Assignment Project Powered Device - Assignment

/en/course/2026/WBVP26PAA.outcomes:
The student can:
Work on projects: executes a project according to the provided project method; delivers the entire final project result as per the assignment; demonstrates effective collaboration to creatively solve a problem and meet deadlines.
Methodically design: designs a conceptual solution following the provided design method.
Apply digital tools: designs using common digital tools.
Construct: substantiates the development of the chosen concept based on relevant theories, including Statics/Applied Mechanics, Drives, and Controls.
Test: conducts physical and digital tests on a single component of the developed solution, formulates an improvement plan based on the results, and implements it; develops the chosen concept based on field-applied guidelines and standards, including the Machinery Directive and drawing standards.
Communicate: communicates clearly both orally and in written form.
Reflect: knows themselves, describes, and substantiates their strengths; dares to ask for feedback and knows how to use the feedback for personal development.
/en/course/2026/WBVP26PAA.content: The student designs and constructs a powered mechanism in a structured manner. They use modern professional tools and demonstrate professional skills. The design is documented according to common standards in a construction dossier.

metadata.Name: Dynamics
metadata.Assessments: Dynamics - Written, organised by STAD examinations Mathematics - Assignment

/en/course/2026/WBVP24DYN.outcomes:
The student:
using a methodical approach¸ determines the acceleration, velocity and distance travelled for the motion of a point mass and/or a rigid body in the plane. This should make use of available kinematic equations. The main emphasis here is on a methodical approach. The result is a clearly documented calculation
relates the acceleration of a point mass and/or a rigid body in the plane to the forces and torques. This should make use of the available equations of motion to ultimately calculate the unknown forces/torques and/or accelerations. The emphasis here is on a methodical approach. The result is a clearly documented calculation based on a VLS and KS
applies the principle of ‘work and energy’ and the ‘law of conservation of mechanical energy’ to issues involving the search for a relationship between external forces, velocities and distance travelled. The unknown data must be calculated. The main emphasis here is on a methodical approach. The result is a clearly documented calculation based on a VLS of a point mass moving in the flat plane that
determines the required mechanical power and efficiency for the movement of a point mass and/or rigid body in the plane. The main emphasis here is on a methodical approach. The result is a clearly documented calculation.
determines the derivative of various functions, graphs it and applies it in determining extremes.
determines the primitive of various functions, applies it in calculating areas and contents of revolutionary bodies.

metadata.Name: Materialiseren & Dimensioneren II
metadata.Assessments: Applied Mechanics - Written, organised by STAD examinations Materials Science - Assignment

/en/course/2026/WBVP24MD2.outcomes:
The student:
calculates the external and internal loads of three-dimensionally loaded composite load-bearing structures and tools.
calculates the internal stresses of simple prismatic beams/shafts for given internal loads and checks their admissibility.
calculates the deflection of composite prismatic beams/shafts.
describes the differences in the physical properties of materials based on differences in their chemical properties.
determines an optimal material for a given application using a systematic method.
checks whether a product fails under buckling load.
/en/course/2026/WBVP24MD2.content: For an engineer, when designing composite structures, it is necessary to check if they meet strength and stiffness requirements. Through this course, internal stresses resulting from loads on composite structures are calculated. The stiffness of simple products is also calculated. This is systematically done using a framework. With knowledge of materials and their properties, a suitable material for construction components is determined.

/en/course/2026/WBVP25CT.outcomes:
The student:
Designs a drive so that the correct displacements (rotation and translation) of moving parts can only occur in the desired directions.
Selects machine parts (such as bearings and gears) for a designed driven device, based on a set of requirements.
Selects a PMDC motor for a given application based on required power, and spatial dimensions.
Calculates a gear ratio to match the load and motor curves and selects a commercially available gear that achieves this.
/en/course/2026/WBVP25CT.content: Within the module Components and Transmissions, students learn how to select and dimension machine parts based on a load and drive (electric motors). They can apply this knowledge in the design and engineering phase of their project. In this project, they design a robot based on this knowledge, in which various components and transmissions will be incorporated.

/en/course/2026/WBVP26DT.outcomes:
The student:
- creates and reads 2D workshop drawing(s) of assemblies, including bills of materials (BOM)
- creates and reads 2D workshop drawing(s) of individual parts (detail drawing(s))
/en/course/2026/WBVP26DT.content:
Mastery of CAD is essential for the modern engineer and forms the basis for design visualization, production planning, and production processes.
In this module, the emphasis is on creating and reading workshop drawing(s) according to NEN and ISO standards.

metadata.Name: Project Energy Systems
metadata.Assessments: Professional Identity - Assignment Project Energy Systems - Assignment

/en/course/2026/WBVB26PRE.outcomes:
The student,
Visualizes the energy flows in an installation with variable demand for heat, cold and power by building a calculation model for a stationary situation
Measures the energy flows in an installation and analyses the obtained data to quantify energy losses
Generates concept solutions (for example with a PFD), places them in the context of the challenges in the energy transition, and assesses the solution by calculating it at the concept level
Dimensions a solution to a level agreed with the client
Organizes and carries out a project according to a suitable method in which components are divided and connected, while each member of the project group maintains an overview of the project and has a clear responsibility
Finds out whether the actual image of the stakeholders (client and manager) corresponds with their image of progress, cooperation, communication, and end results
Collects feedback regarding the intended and performed tasks and then reflects on this
/en/course/2026/WBVB26PRE.content: During this project, an energy system in the process industry or installation technology is designed or optimized to achieve energy savings. The project is preferably carried out for an external client, ultimately requiring an advisory report to be delivered with detailed improvement proposals.

metadata.Name: Introduction Energy
metadata.Assessments: Introduction Energy - Computer, organised by STAD examinations

/en/course/2026/WBVB24IE.content: The course explores the growing demand for energy and the need to use fossil fuels more efficiently and sustainably, following the principles of the trias energetica. Students study thermodynamics, gas laws, and cycle processes to understand how chemical energy in closed systems is converted into work. They analyze current and future energy transitions in the Netherlands, calculate energetic efficiency and CO₂ impacts of more sustainable alternatives, and represent state changes in pV‑diagrams. Students also describe idealized processes (isentropic, isobaric, isothermal) and propose efficiency improvements. A hands‑on bicycle pump practicum reinforces the theoretical concepts.

metadata.Name: Energy generation
metadata.Assessments: Energy generation - Written, organised by STAD examinations

/en/course/2026/WBVB24EOP.outcomes:
De student,
applies mass and energy balances to heat or cold generating installations.
draws the process of heat or cold generation in a diagram (such as log p-h, T-s and H-s)
calculates a heat or cold generation process with regard to temperatures, pressures and efficiencies.
determines the effect of changing process parameters (such as temperature, pressure & flow) on the performance of the installation.
selects a heat or cold source based on desired power and efficiency.

/en/course/2026/WBVB24ETR.outcomes:
The student:
calculates pressure differences and flows in hydraulic systems using Bernoulli's law and the continuity equation.
calculates losses due to major and minor factors within the system.
interprets basic hydraulic circuits, including series and parallel piping networks
selects appropriate displacement or centrifugal pumps and interpret/apply their parameters and characteristics
describes the working principles of hydraulic and pneumatic systems and components
calculates pressures, forces, powers, and energy of hydraulic components within a given hydraulic system
analyses the operation of a hydraulic system from a schematic representation and additional information, supported by relevant calculations.
/en/course/2026/WBVB24ETR.content:
In this comprehensive course, we delve into the world of fluid carrying systems with a focus on design considerations. From specifying system requirements to ensuring alignment with desired behaviours, we explore the application of key equations such as the Bernoulli equation, Darcy-Weissbach equation, and Moody diagrams. The investigation of Reynolds numbers and their correlation to laminar and turbulent flow is a key aspect. The hydraulic networks, encompassing both series and parallel piping systems, are thoroughly studied.
The course extends its reach to actuators found in various processes and machines, with a particular emphasis on hydraulic and pneumatic actuators. Hydraulic actuators are renowned for their precision and absolute force delivery, while pneumatic drives play a crucial role in control systems, manipulating the state of components like switches. The course addresses essential questions such as the structure of a complete drive system, the design process based on requirements and calculations, and the modelling of drive systems through schematization.

/en/course/2026/WBVB24EOV.outcomes:
The student:
calculates, draws, and explains the temperature distribution and heat flow through multiple layers of material (plate and tube; conduction and convection)
determines the heat transfer coefficient for convection based on characteristic numbers
calculates temperatures and powers in a heat exchanger with heat capacity flows, logarithmic mean temperature differences, and power balances
selects and sizes components (underfloor heating and radiators) appropriate for the required heat output
/en/course/2026/WBVB24EOV.content: Many mechanical installations and machines transfer heat. Sometimes that is precisely the purpose, sometimes heat is a byproduct. Transfer occurs through radiation, conduction, and convection. This course covers the theory of transfer in static situations. Calculating and sizing heat exchangers is applied to radiators and underfloor heating.

metadata.Name: Project Product Design and Industrialization
metadata.Assessments: English - Assignment Professional Identity - Assignment Project - Assignment Reporting - Assignment

/en/course/2026/WBVB23PPI.content:
The module focuses on the integrated understanding, analysis, and optimization of industrial production processes within the context of Smart Industry. Attention is paid to the interrelationship between product design, production preparation, production organization, cost price determination, and process optimization.
The course addresses the core concepts and current developments in smart industry, such as the digitalization of production processes, automation, data‑driven decision-making, and the integration of humans, machines, and information. Students learn to comprehend the complexity of modern production systems and to place them within technological, organizational, and economic frameworks.

/en/course/2026/WBVB24MSE.outcomes:
The student can:
Translate the properties of a driven system into a load characteristic.
Derive a motor characteristic from the motor parameters, calculate the optimal operating point based on motor and load characteristics.
Select a motor based on information about the load characteristic and desired speed and calculate the power consumption and efficiency.
Dimension shafts, calculate whether a shaft is strong enough, and ensure that the shaft does not exceed fatigue limits under (dynamic) loading.
Select the appropriate machine components (e.g., bearings and belt drives) in conjunction with the correct fits and lubricants.
/en/course/2026/WBVB24MSE.content:
During this 5 ECTS module, an existing machine is used as a "framework" to study several topics. Initially, the machine is used for a "reverse engineering" step. What are the specifications of the various components, and why are these components used? The parts that make up the drivetrain receive the most attention. After analysing the existing machine, an upgrade of the drivetrain must be engineered. This includes selecting an electric motor, several machine components (bearings, belt drives), and dimensioning the drive or support shaft, all for changed operating conditions. The following topics are covered:
Selecting electric motors (AC and DC) for a drivetrain.
Dimensioning shafts. This involves simplifying the situation from 3D to 2D by using vector summation of moments.
Fatigue of shafts: Various factors influencing fatigue are discussed here. The static and dynamic checks for fatigue take all these factors into account.
Rolling bearings: Different types of rolling bearings and determining a suitable rolling bearing for a specific situation.
Belt drives: Different types of belt drives with a focus on belts and the corresponding belt types and calculations.

/en/course/2026/WBVB26MDC-NL.content:
Operations management is the branch of management that defines the complete production timeline of a service/ product from the input stage to the finished stage, including planning, organizing, and supervising the operations, manufacturing and production processes, and service delivery to lead to the desired goals. We will discuss the factors that are important for the design of a process. Concerning the planning and control of operations, topics include capacity management, inventory management and scheduling. Finally, several improvement methods, like Lean Manufacturing and Six Sigma are treated.
Data and data management is the backbone of a production origanisation. Within a company, information is used in various ways to achieve a working and controllable (production) process. We will learn about the different information systems. These are the systems where data related to a product, process, and business is collected in order to generate and share information within the company.  In more detail: data and documentation management, product document management, product lifecycle management (PLM), Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) systems and the Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT). This module consists of theory of information models, database systems applied in (manufacturing) companies and practical assignment within the Windchill PLM system.

/en/course/2026/WBVB25CDE-NL.content: In this module, you will learn how to systematically approach design throughout the entire product lifecycle and understand why this is a valuable addition to the quick, inventive approach. Through systems theory, you will learn to identify relationships between subsystems and their functions and to think at different levels. After the design and production phases, you will gain deeper insights into maintenance and management and material choice. By systematically addressing design and maintenance throughout the product lifecycle, students will be equipped with the skills necessary to create efficient, sustainable, and high-quality products.

/en/course/2026/WBVB25SPC-NL.outcomes:
The student:
Collects data for a statistical analysis where the data is described graphically (for example using a histogram) and numerically (for example using a measure for central tendency or spread) using a digital tool (for example Excel, Minitab, or Python).
Describes a collection of population using discrete (such as the binomial or Poisson distribution) and continuous probability distributions (such as the normal distribution) and can make statistical statements about it.3. Determines confidence intervals for the mean and standard deviation and makes a statement about a population and/or sample size.
Investigate with (linear) regression analysis the relationship between two variables in a small data set
Determines, based on measured quality criteria, whether a production process is technically and statistically controlled
By using samples from a production line, draw up control charts for the average, deviation, or a discrete criterion and, based on the control charts, provide advice on whether production needs to be adjusted.
/en/course/2026/WBVB25SPC-NL.content: In (mass) production processes, controlling the process is crucial for the quality of the products. Controlling processes requires knowledge about variation that will always be present. This variation can be displayed and taken into account using statistics. With a self-collected dataset, topics from descriptive statistics are discussed. In addition, with inferential statistics static statements will be made about the sample and population. Finally, a production process will be analyzed in which statements are made as to whether the process is statistically and technically controlled and whether the process may need to be adjusted to have sufficiently low failure rates.

/en/course/2026/WBVB25STGVT.content: During his internship, the student contributes to current affairs within a mechanical engineering context. This can be done by working on one large assignment or multiple sub-assignments. Thus the internship will enable the student to become familiar with his future work environment.

metadata.Name: Project Research, Design, Engineering or Maintenance
metadata.Language: Dutch, with parts in English, English
metadata.Assessments: Professional Skills - Assignment Project Research, Design, Engineering or Maintenance - Assignment

/en/course/2026/WBVB26PRDE.content: In this project (10 EC) a professional mechanical engineering problem is addressed. The subject contains product as well as system issues. During the project the entire engineering process is addressed. First, an analysis of the problem including a literature research will be performed. Subsequently, a solution to the problem will be methodically designed and constructed according to specifications that also take into account the required maintenance. The project will be performed in close cooperation with the client.

metadata.Name: Research & Development
metadata.Language: Dutch, with parts in English, English

/en/course/2026/WBVB25RD.outcomes:
The student:
can analyse a technical-analytical system and draw up a schematic model in which all relevant physical parameters are quantified.
Can describe the operation of a technical system using relevant mechanical engineering equations (mechanics, electrical engineering, thermodynamics, etc.) and model this in a spreadsheet or simulation environment.
Can design and execute an experiment or test to determine and quantify the influence of individual parameters.
Can execute an experiment in a structured and reproducible manner and collect data that is relevant, reliable and suitable for further analysis.
Can report the results of both theoretical and experimental research clearly and formulate substantiated conclusions and recommendations in a technical report.
/en/course/2026/WBVB25RD.content:
In the R&D module, the analysis, modelling and testing of functional systems will be studied. The learning outcomes  describe the competencies that are expected of the student when conducting both theoretical and practical research within R&D.
The student learns to view systems from a systematic and practical perspective, in which both the theoretical foundation and the practical execution of experiments are important. Drawing up models, conducting calculations and simulations, and validating results by means of experiments are essential components of this.
The results are used to analyze technical problems and to devise and sunstantiate new solutions to the problem. In doing so, the student is expected to collect and process data in a structured and reproducible manner and to report the findings clearly in a technical report.

/en/course/2026/WBVB25AR.outcomes:
The student:
can develop, build and debug digital control programs for simple industrial installations using Boolean algebra
analyses a simple industrial installation and develop a control logic for that
uses different logical functions for the control program such as and-, or-, not-, memory-, time- and counter-functions
can draw control diagrams and defend the design
programs PLC’s using ladder logic and sequential function chart and/or structured text language
can make a sequential function chart program for a simple industrial installation
/en/course/2026/WBVB25AR.content: In this 5 EC-course the student learns about digital control programs for industrial installations. The student learns the fundamentals of digital electronics and programming, digital input and output devices, programming methods, ladder logic and other control diagrams. The theory will be enhanced with programming exercises at industrial plc’s.

/en/course/2026/WBVB26MC.outcomes:
Learning outcome 1: System analysis
The student can: analyse a technical production or energy system by identifying the relevant input, process and output parameters and defining the system boundary.
Explanation: This involves understanding how a system works, what variables affect it, and how they interact.
Learning outcome 2: Modelling systems
The student can establish a model structure of a production or energy system and translate it into a mathematical or data-driven model.
Note: Consider setting up equations, block diagrams or using any software tools.
Learning outcome 3: Data acquisition and sensor integration
The student can collect relevant data from an existing system using sensors and measurement systems, and process this data for analysis.
Note: This includes the use of measurement instruments, data logging and understanding signal processing.
Learning outcome 4: Predicting system behaviour and product quality
Based on a model and collected data, the student can make predictions about the behaviour of the system and/or the quality of the product produced.
Explanation: For example, predicting failures, deviations in product quality or energy consumption.
Learning outcome 5: Critical reflection and optimisation
The student can evaluate the performance of the model, explain deviations and suggest optimisation of the system or model.
Explanation: This promotes critical thinking and the ability to improve models based on real-world data.
/en/course/2026/WBVB26MC.content:
Analysis and modelling of production systems, predicting the behaviour of systems (process scharacteristics/product quality)
This module deals with describing, analysing and modelling energy and/or production systems and/or the resulting products. Modelling systems starts with a model structure of the system. It defines the input and output of the system and how to build a relationship between the input and output parameters. Sensors and data collection from an existing system are used to predict system behaviour and/or product quality.

metadata.Name: Installation Engineering
metadata.Language: Dutch, with parts in English, English

/en/course/2026/WBVB25IB.outcomes:
The student:
Applies the Mollier h-x chart to design processes for conditioning air, and calculates the associated cooling, heating, drying and moistening duties.
Calculates inlet air conditions and flow required to maintain a required room condition.
Explains the effect of control valves and check valves on flow distribution, pressure differences over valves, heat transfer and temperatures within a hydronic system with varying duty.
Selects valves (kvs) with appropriate authority while minimizing pump power and calculates target pressure differences across valves.
Interprets and designs the modular hydronic structure and checks for its correct functioning.
/en/course/2026/WBVB25IB.content:
This course provides the basics of HVAC (Heating, Ventilation and Air Conditioning) installation design and engineering for climate control in buildings. The design process starts at climate requirements and heating/cooling duties. The process ends with the design of the hydraulic system and dimensioning of valves and piping. An overview is provided of distribution systems and components to deliver heat, cold and fresh air.
This course deals with air treatment installations and heat delivery systems, but not with the generation of heat and cold (chillers, heat pumps, CHP, heat/cold storage, boilers, etc.). Much attention will be given to the hydronic design (parallel circuits with headers, pipes, control valves and balancing valves), which is key to energy efficiency of installations and comfort of people in buildings. The provided knowledge on hydronic systems is also relevant for understanding and designing industrial process installations, district heating systems and for efficient operation of heat pumps.

metadata.Name: Machine Engineering
metadata.Language: Dutch, with parts in English, English

/en/course/2026/WBVB25MB.content: In this 5 EC module, an existing machine is used as a means to study a number of subjects. ‘Guide to application of the Machinery Directive 2006/42/EC’ is used to analyse the machine. Moreover, a risk-analysis (FMEA) is performed to show all current problems, malfunctions and/or hazards of the existing machine. A number of engineering skills are used, such as selection of machine parts (brakes, clutches, gears, etc.), determining the applicable load cases in a dynamic situation and strength/strain calculations for machine parts and sub-assemblies using FEM-software in the worst case situation.

metadata.Name: Graduation Project
metadata.Language: Dutch, with parts in English, English

/en/course/2026/WBVB25AFS.outcomes: In the graduation project, you will prove that you are competent at a B.Sc. level and that you are ready to enter the field as a starting professional. Under the Teaching and Examination Regulation (TER) you can find information on the competency levels, skills and attitudes (TER: Behaviour characteristics).

metadata.Name: Research Innovation Potentials
metadata.Assessments: 3D tekenen - Assignment Hydraulische aandrijving - Computer, organised by STAD examinations Methode van Onderzoek - Assignment Project HTSM TB/W - Assignment Sterkteleer 2 - Computer, organised by STAD examinations

metadata.Name: Project Prototype
metadata.Assessments: Professional skills - Assignment Project Prototype - Assignment

/en/course/2026/WBVP26PP.outcomes:
The student:
can define the problem statement, objectives and client's requirements for a business project in which a machine or tool will be designed, engineered and built
creates a new design in the context of a business project by applying tools and methods accepted in practice
in the context of a business project, the student can further elaborate the result from the design phase into a fully dimensioned product and subsequently realize a prototype of this product by applying tools and methods accepted in practice
for a monodisciplinary project, the student can draw up a plan or approach with which the content of the project is determined and structured and with which the workload and task distribution of the project members is determined and adjusted where necessary
communicates effectively with a client regarding  technical issues in a manner accepted in the professional field
works in a self-chosen role with colleagues to achieve project objectives and evaluates the results achieved in the light of the set goals
/en/course/2026/WBVP26PP.content:
This course offers a hands-on learning experience concentrated around the design and construction of an electric motor-driven mechanical solution.
Students will engage in creating a device with moving components such as shafts and bearings, addressing mechanical challenges like strength, bending, shear, and fatigue. The course emphasizes practical problem-solving, with students developing a proof of concept through techniques like welding, machining, and forming, culminating in a design review presentation.
Throughout the semester, the project will evolve in tandem with modules teaching technical and social skills relevant to each phase. Workshop techniques, including turning, milling, waterjet cutting, sheet metal forming, and welding, will be integral to the curriculum, especially in the later weeks. The course includes mandatory activities like project meetings, design and engineering reviews, prototype demonstrations, workshop training, and skill development classes. The students, as a group, will start with analysing the chosen technical problem using the "Methodical design method". During this period, information regarding topics such as the plan of approach, project organization, workshop skills, and portfolio making will be acquired. During the design and engineering stage, the student presents solutions and practices skills by advising an actual client. Ultimately, the client will give a "Go-No-go" decision to a proposed solution.
Although the project is a group effort with a common goal, individual roles will also be assigned. These roles may include project manager, chairman, minute taker, planner, and mechanical lead engineer. It's up to the group to divide the roles and evenly distribute the workload amongst each other regarding the project tasks.
Overall, the project aims to provide a comprehensive learning experience that combines theoretical knowledge with practical skills, allowing students to develop their personal and professional competencies.

/en/course/2026/WBVP26CAD.outcomes:
1. CAD Modelling (Assignments 1 & 2) Students can create fully defined 3D part models using sketches, features, relations, and dimensions; build multi-part assemblies with correct mates and a clean part structure; resolve incomplete or contradictory drawings by interpreting engineering intent; and produce simple 2D workshop drawings including BOM and position numbers.
2. Motion Simulation (Assignment 3) Students can set up a correct Motion Study to drive a mechanism using a motor or force input; generate realistic time-dependent reaction forces and displacement plots; and export the reaction forces required for structural FEA.
3. Structural Simulation (Assignment 4) Students can apply realistic boundary conditions using degrees of freedom (DOF), particularly cylindrical fixtures (radial, axial, rotational); apply force data from the Motion Study to a structural model; run an FEA on an assembly and create a sub-model with a refined mesh; and interpret stress plots, displacement, and potential weak regions in the design.
4. ISO Technical Drawings (Assignment 5) Students can produce fully annotated 2D technical drawings to ISO standards, including correct dimensioning, tolerances, views, and title block; and present their design clearly and professionally.
/en/course/2026/WBVP26CAD.content:
3D CAD is essential for producing technical drawings, running simulations, supporting sustainability analysis, and presenting designs professionally. Drafting skills, ISO standards in particular, remain the professional language of engineering communication.
The five subjects:
Basics of 3D CAD
– Sketch → feature → part → assembly.
First Model
– Create your first usable model (tutorial + can crusher).
Simulation: Motion
– Test how it moves; kinematics, forces, torque.
Simulation: FEM
– Check whether the design is structurally sound.
ISO Drafting
– Dimensioning, tolerances, advanced CAD, and technical presentations.

metadata.Name: Applied Mechanics
metadata.Assessments: Applied Mechanics - Written, organised by STAD examinations

/en/course/2026/WBVP23AM1.outcomes:
The student:
translates a given 2-dimensional statically loaded product into a schematic representation and translates this schematic representation further into Free Body Diagram (FBD)
determines the unknown external loads by applying the three laws of equilibrium in a structured manner
determines the internal loads of a construction using the method of sections
calculates internal stresses from the internal loads using a set of given relations
compares the maximum internals stress to the maximum stress acceptable by the material
solves mathematical equations that are relevant for the engineering field
/en/course/2026/WBVP23AM1.content: All products around us have been designed to fulfill certain requirements. In many cases, the dominant design aspects are related to strength requirements. In this course (5 EC), the student will learn to translate external loads into internal loads and stresses, and check the strength of the material. Analyses of given practical situations will be performed in a structured manner. Relevant mathematics will be taught along the way.

metadata.Name: Design Engineering
metadata.Assessments: Design Engineering - Written, organised by STAD examinations

/en/course/2026/WBVP23DE.outcomes:
The student:
Can apply methodical design principles to systematically structure and guide the engineering design process.
Can conduct user research to identify needs and incorporate them into the design strategy.
Can select and dimension mechanical components such as bearings, shafts, and belts based on engineering standards and calculations.
Can analyze and visualize product functionality using tools like functional decomposition and MEI diagrams.
Can calculate and evaluate power transmission systems including belt, chain, and gear drives for mechanical applications.
Can apply basic tribological knowledge to design plain and rolling bearings with suitable materials and lubrication methods.
Can assess fatigue and stress concentrations to ensure safe and durable shaft designs under cyclic loads.
Can interpret and apply basic electric motor data to select motors that meet specific torque, speed, and efficiency requirements.
Can justify and defend design decisions using requirement lists, decision matrices, and performance analyses.
Can iteratively improve a design through prototyping, testing, and incorporating feedback into the development process.
/en/course/2026/WBVP23DE.content:
Design |
Part of the Design & Engineering lectures, utilizing the "Design Handbook" (Zeiler). Upon completing this component, students will gain the ability to comprehend and apply methodical design principles, conduct user research, analyze product functionality, draft problem statements, visualize solutions through diagrams, objectively select the optimal solution, and effectively defend their design choices.
Engineering |
Part of the Design & Engineering lectures, using "Machine Elements in Mechanical Design" (Mott).
Upon completing this component, students will acquire the skills necessary to design mechanical drive systems, select appropriate components, perform essential calculations, and troubleshoot potential issues. This knowledge will empower them to contribute to the creation of reliable and efficient mechanical systems in various engineering applications.

/en/course/2026/WBVP23MT.outcomes:
Student is able to:
describe the machining operations of turning, milling, drilling, and threading, along with the corresponding tools
select, based on given technical drawings, material, type of cutting material, and type of operations, the following data from tables: feed rate, cutting speed, specific cutting force, and tool life for turning and threading operations
select, based on given technical drawings, material, type of cutting material, and type of operations, the following data from tables: feed rate, cutting speed, and tool life for milling operations
calculate parameters such as cutting depth, speed, operations time, main cutting force, and net required power for turning operations using the provided data
calculate parameters such as cutting depth, speed, and operations time for milling operations using the provided data
describe the processes of joining and forming, with a particular focus on welding, bolting, bonding, soldering and casting, including their specific characteristics.
calculate the unfolded length, minimum bend radius, maximum bend radius, free bending force, die bending force, and punch-through force of bending operations such as air bending, swivel bending, and die bending based on technical drawings
calculate punch force, edge and center distances, strip width, and punch hole dimensional accuracy for punching operations based on technical drawings
calculate parameters like blank diameter, draw ratio, number of draws, draw force, and die holder pressure for deep drawing operations based on technical drawings
/en/course/2026/WBVP23MT.content: In this course, students will acquire valuable insights into product manufacturing by exploring a diverse range of machining processes, techniques, and machinery. They will develop the capacity to analyse and compute crucial parameters for operations like turning, milling, drilling, and threading, while also comprehending the broader implications of operation durations and costs. Furthermore, students will delve into the realm of product fabrication through non-machining avenues, encompassing techniques, machinery, and welding methods. They will master the ability to ascertain and calculate vital parameters for various operations and techniques, thereby cultivating a holistic comprehension of operation durations and associated costs.

metadata.Name: Project Energy Systems
metadata.Assessments: Professional Identity - Assignment Project Energy Systems - Assignment

/en/course/2026/WBVP26PES.outcomes:
Student is able to:
understand the unique challenges associated with building energy in church buildings, including architectural and historical considerations
identify and collect relevant data on church building energy performance, such as energy bills, equipment specifications, and building characteristics
analyze and interpret energy data using appropriate methods, such as regression analysis, energy modelling, and simulation
evaluate the energy efficiency of the church building and identify opportunities for improvement, including measures related to building envelope, HVAC, lighting, and occupant behavior
design and evaluate various energy efficiency measures using technical and economic analysis methods, and select the most appropriate measures based on energy savings, cost effectiveness, and other relevant criteria
develop a comprehensive report and presentation that summarizes the church building energy performance analysis, including recommendations for energy efficiency improvements, estimated energy savings, and economic analysis results
communicate effectively with stakeholders, such as church leaders, congregation members, and engineering professionals, to present the results of the church building energy analysis project and discuss potential energy efficiency measures
apply critical thinking and problem-solving skills to address challenges and uncertainties in the church building energy analysis process, and make data-driven decisions based on available information
understand the role of building energy analysis in the context of sustainability, and recognize the importance of reducing energy use and greenhouse gas emissions in the built environment, including in historic and cultural buildings such as churches
/en/course/2026/WBVP26PES.content: This project focuses on the energy and system analysis of a certain building or location which needs to be made sustainable. Within the project, the students, as a group, will perform an analysis of chosen technical problem or case study. During this phase the students will receive just-in-time information.  Understanding of the heat transfer concepts and energy flows are a pre-requisite in order to perform a system analysis, these topics will be addressed in the Fluid mechanics (WBVP23FM), Heat transfer (WBVP23HT) and Thermodynamics (WBVP23TD). In the end the students submit an advisory technical report as a deliverable to the client.

metadata.Name: Fluid Mechanics
metadata.Assessments: Fluid Mechanics - Written, organised by STAD examinations

/en/course/2026/WBVP23FM.outcomes:
The student:
calculates pressure differences and flows in hydraulic systems using Bernoulli's law and the continuity equation
calculates losses due to major and minor factors within the system
interprets basic hydraulic circuits, including series and parallel piping networks
selects appropriate displacement or centrifugal pumps and interpret/apply their parameters and characteristics
describes the working principles of hydraulic and pneumatic systems and components
calculates pressures, forces, powers, and energy of hydraulic components within a given hydraulic system
analyzes the operation of a hydraulic system from a schematic representation and additional information, supported by relevant calculations
/en/course/2026/WBVP23FM.content: In this comprehensive course, we delve into the world of fluid carrying systems with a focus on design considerations. From specifying system requirements to ensuring alignment with desired behaviours, we explore the application of key equations such as the Bernoulli equation, Darcy-Weissbach equation, and Moody diagrams. The investigation of Reynolds numbers and their correlation to laminar and turbulent flow is a key aspect. The hydraulic networks, encompassing both series and parallel piping systems, are thoroughly studied. The course extends its reach to actuators found in various processes and machines, with a particular emphasis on hydraulic and pneumatic actuators. Hydraulic actuators are renowned for their precision and absolute force delivery, while pneumatic drives play a crucial role in control systems, manipulating the state of components like switches. The course addresses essential questions such as the structure of a complete drive system, the design process based on requirements and calculations, and the modelling of drive systems through schematization. Throughout lectures, literature, and examinations, the primary focus is on hydraulic design, with attention given to pneumatic systems and their similarities and differences in the laboratory work. This course equips students with a profound understanding of fluid systems and actuators, offering valuable insights for designing, modelling, and optimizing these systems for real-world applications.

metadata.Name: Thermodynamics
metadata.Assessments: Thermodynamics - Written, organised by STAD examinations

/en/course/2026/WBVP23TD.outcomes:
The student:
explains the 1st and 2nd laws of thermodynamics for closed and open systems to converting heat into work in internal combustion engines
understands the various gas laws and equations of state and apply them to solve problems of gas mixtures in estimating enthalpy, entropy, specific heat and internal energy
calculates the effect of changes to the engine on the thermodynamic efficiency and power and relates these calculations to the P-V diagram
draws a circuit process of a given cooling/heating configuration and can derive states, state magnitudes and phase transitions from a log p-h diagram
can calculate through different system configurations such as: cascade, multi-stage compression, multiple evaporators/condensers, flash tank, and intercooler
knows how to calculate and improve the COP of a given system
describes the working principles of adsorption cooling
/en/course/2026/WBVP23TD.content: Thermodynamics is a 5.0 EC course deals with the equations of state, the first law of thermodynamics, second law of thermodynamics, p-V diagrams, ideal gas (Boyle-Gay-Lussac). This further deals with physical principles behind energy conversions in machines, and provides the foundation for calculations on power and efficiency. We will study the machines where a continuous gas flow running through it, which can be viewed only as an open system. Particularly in components such as pumps, turbines and nozzles, and to systems such as gas turbines (this could be applied in aircraft, helicopters, power plants). The course furthermore focuses on applying the above mentioned thermodynamic principles in analyzing and assessing compression/absorption cooling cycles and heat pumps. Compression/absorption cooling is widely used in various branches like the food industry, (industrial) refrigerators and freezers, HVAC, liquefying natural gas, etc. Heat pumps are mainly used as a sustainable way for heating residential houses, buildings, office spaces, but also in industry. The students will be able to perform (simple) design calculations and determine the efficiency of the systems by means of the coefficient of performance. Lastly students will be able to critically analyze these systems and provide advice on methods for efficiency improvement

metadata.Name: Heat Transfer
metadata.Assessments: Heat Transfer - Written, organised by STAD examinations

/en/course/2026/WBVP23HT.outcomes:
The student:
calculates, draws, and explains the temperature distribution and heat flow through multiple layers of material (plate and tube; conduction and convection)
determines the heat transfer coefficient for convection based on characteristic numbers
calculates temperatures and powers in a heat exchanger with heat capacity flows, logarithmic mean temperature differences, and power balances
selects and sizes components (underfloor heating and radiators) appropriate for the required heat output.
/en/course/2026/WBVP23HT.content: Many mechanical installations and machines transfer heat. Sometimes that is precisely the purpose, sometimes heat is a byproduct. Transfer occurs through radiation, conduction, and convection. This course covers the theory of transfer in static situations. Calculating and sizing heat exchangers is applied to radiators and underfloor heating.

/en/course/2026/WBVP26ENG.outcomes:
Communicate technical engineering concepts effectively in English by explaining complex systems, manufacturing processes, project constraints, and technical decisions to both specialist and non-specialist audiences using precise, industry-appropriate language.
Demonstrate professional communication skills in international engineering contexts by participating confidently in meetings, presentations, negotiations, and client interactions, using appropriate strategies for persuasion, managing expectations, diplomatic disagreement, and collaborative decision-making.
Speak English with increased clarity and professional fluency by applying appropriate pronunciation, intonation, and discourse strategies, reducing common Dutch pronunciation patterns and using effective turn-taking techniques in multicultural workplace communication.
/en/course/2026/WBVP26ENG.content:
Format and assessment:
Preparation and workshops. Students can obtain the credits If all preparations have been completed at a sufficient level and all classes have been taken. If these criteria have not been met at the end of the series of workshops, students can take an oral exam to prove their skills.
Content and learning goals
High-level English for engineers aims to improve the students’ communication by shifting from functional to persuasive and precise, industry-specific language. Targeted professional communication will focus on learning how to deal with workplace-related skills, such as negotiating specifications, explaining complex systems clearly without using overly technical jargon, presenting to executives, describing cause and effect, defining failure consequences, outlining manufacturing processes, discussing project constraints, timelines, and resources with management or contractors and managing client expectations.
Cultural and professional fluency is required to participate and lead international teams. Learning how to diplomatically challenge a co-worker or client, without sounding aggressive or admissive. Practical skills like knowing how to interrupt politely, taking the floor during global cross-functional meetings.
Pronunciation mistakes that are typically made by Dutch speakers of English will be addressed to minimize a Dutch accent when speaking English.

/en/course/2026/WBVB24PDI.content:
Designing and drawing a product is one thing, but then producing it is another step. The questions that can be asked are: how is the part made? Which machines are available? In what order will we produce? What will be the cost price of the product? What will be the delivery time?
All these questions are addressed in this project. It is (therefore) a next step in the product creation process. This section is about the work preparation/planning/delivery time to get from drawing to product.
Often, with new products, a prototype is first made to remove all minor (production) errors and only then does series production proceed. Within this project we will do something similar; first prepare the work preparation/planning/delivery time for prototypes in an existing production environment and then prepare the work preparation/planning/delivery time for the series in an optimized line (own design).

/en/course/2026/WBVB24DRE.outcomes:
The student:
solves kinematic problems of particles or rigid bodies, involving displacement, velocity, and acceleration, by using the relevant kinematic equations
solves kinetic problems of particles or rigid bodies, involving forces and moments, by using the relevant equations of motion or the "principle of work and energy"
calculates the required mechanical power and energy losses of a driven system
translates the properties of a driven system into a load characteristic and selects an AC-motor based on information of the load characteristic and the desired speed and calculates the power consumption and efficiency
translates a given three dimensional statically loaded assembly into schematic representations and Free Body diagrams (FBD) of the individual parts and determines the external and internal loads of the parts for statically determined and undetermined cases
optimises the cross-sectional area of a three-dimensional loaded part (F.e. shaft) by fulfilling strength and stiffness requirements

/en/course/2026/WBVB26MDC-EN.content:
Operations management is the branch of management that defines the complete production timeline of a service/ product from the input stage to the finished stage, including planning, organizing, and supervising the operations, manufacturing and production processes, and service delivery to lead to the desired goals. We will discuss the factors that are important for the design of a process. Concerning the planning and control of operations, topics include capacity management, inventory management and scheduling. Finally, several improvement methods, like Lean Manufacturing and Six Sigma are treated.
Data and data management is the backbone of a production origanisation. Within a company, information is used in various ways to achieve a working and controllable (production) process. We will learn about the different information systems. These are the systems where data related to a product, process, and business is collected in order to generate and share information within the company.  In more detail: data and documentation management, product document management, product lifecycle management (PLM), Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) systems and the Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT). This module consists of theory of information models, database systems applied in (manufacturing) companies and practical assignment within the Windchill PLM system.

/en/course/2026/WBVB25CDE-EN.outcomes:
The student:
conducts an analysis of the user and the use scenario to develop a set of requirements
applies system approach for analyzing the main function of a product
understands the LCA (life cycle analysis) during product design
describes the functions of the components in the installation based on system analysis
applies principles of circular design in product design, material selection and end of life management while ensuring a realistic business case
determines the maintenance needs by selecting from different maintenance models
designs measures to reduce the risks of failure based on a self-conducted FMECA linked to a risk matrix
sets up a maintenance plan for a specific asset, focusing on costs (TCO), efficiency, and quality, (based on a maintenance vision and strategy)
acquires knowledge of materials, their composition, application areas, and recyclability, and applies this knowledge to the design process.
/en/course/2026/WBVB25CDE-EN.content:
In this module, you will learn how to systematically approach design throughout the entire product lifecycle and understand why this is a valuable addition to the quick, inventive approach. Through principles of circular design, you will learn to approach the design of a product to ensure the materials are used in a circular manner, not a linear (make-use-waste) method.
After the design and production phases, you will gain deeper insights into maintenance and management and material choice. By systematically addressing circular design and maintenance throughout the product lifecycle, students will be equipped with the skills necessary to create efficient, sustainable, and high-quality products.

/en/course/2026/WBVB25SPC-EN.outcomes:
The student:
Collects data for a statistical analysis where the data is described graphically (for example using a histogram) and numerically (for example using a measure for central tendency or spread) using a digital tool (for example Excel, Minitab, or Python).
Describes a collection of population using discrete (such as the binomial or Poisson distribution) and continuous probability distributions (such as the normal distribution) and can make statistical statements about it.3. Determines confidence intervals for the mean and standard deviation and makes a statement about a population and/or sample size.
Investigate with (linear) regression analysis the relationship between two variables in a small data set
Determines, based on measured quality criteria, whether a production process is technically and statistically controlled
By using samples from a production line, draw up control charts for the average, deviation, or a discrete criterion and, based on the control charts, provide advice on whether production needs to be adjusted.
/en/course/2026/WBVB25SPC-EN.content: In (mass) production processes, controlling the process is crucial for the quality of the products. Controlling processes requires knowledge about variation that will always be present. This variation can be displayed and taken into account using statistics. With a self-collected dataset, topics from descriptive statistics are discussed. In addition, with inferential statistics static statements will be made about the sample and population. Finally, a production process will be analyzed in which statements are made as to whether the process is statistically and technically controlled and whether the process may need to be adjusted to have sufficiently low failure rates.

CM
In this phase, exploration is central. You write and produce music in a variety of contexts, such as composition, media, songwriting, and production. The assignments provide guidance in developing your emerging craftsmanship. You collect your work and feedback in a portfolio and demonstrate that you have taken a first step toward your own artistic “voice.”
Windband
You develop your instrumental and artistic skills through your main subject, secondary subject, practical classes, theory, and internship/work-based learning. You apply professional knowledge in basic professional situations, explore your artistic identity, and collaborate on artistic projects. In addition, you practice communicating, presenting, and giving simple lessons within your field.

Choir
You develop your conducting skills through a practice choir and supporting vocal lessons. You work with core repertoire and perform it in familiar contexts. You connect your artistic vision to the repertoire, develop collaboration and communication skills, and learn to respond to the needs of your musical environment.

/en/course/2026/HVMP26BVZA1.outcomes:
Area of Expertise and Learning Outcome(s)
1. Clinical reasoning and arguing– Level 1
LOL 1.1 – BVZ-A – N1 – Authentic (DT)
The student justifies and provides care, partly under supervision, in moderately complex authentic care situations, in accordance with the prevailing nursing philosophy and based on clinical reasoning within the nursing process. This is carried out in accordance with the methods, guidelines and (legal) frameworks provided, whilst encouraging the care recipient’s self-management in a manner appropriate to the situation.
LOL 1.2 - BVZ - N1 - Authentic (VLPs & DT)
The student uses, partly under supervision, the communication tools provided to communicate in a person-centred and professional manner with the care recipient, their relatives and other healthcare professionals within a moderately complex authentic situation, in order to encourage self-management.
Indicators
Description
1.2 Works in accordance with standards, guidelines and protocols (BN2030).
1.1 Establishes the nursing process based on provided theories and classifications relating to clinical reasoning, and makes decisions based on the steps of EBP and relevant legislation and regulations (BN2030).
1.3 Supports care recipients in vulnerable situations in promoting self-management, drawing on provided models, theories and tools (BN2030).
1.4 Provides care based on a provided nursing philosophy (BN2030).
1.5 Applies provided models and methodologies to communication within the nursing process (BN2030).
1.6 Communicates during conversations at both the content and relationship levels (BN2030).
1.7 Assesses the effects of their own verbal and non-verbal expressions during conversations (BN2030).
/en/course/2026/HVMP26BVZA1.content:
The course begins with an introduction to the nursing profession. Key topics include: the history of nursing, the nursing code of practice, the nursing philosophy, the nursing professional profile, relevant legislation and regulations, and collaboration with other disciplines. The aim is for students to be able to describe what nursing entails, how the nursing profession differs from other disciplines, and what this means for their own development as a nurse.
Subsequently, in this course, students develop skills within the nursing process to strengthen self-management among care recipients and their loved ones. Students learn to apply methodologies and classifications, such as NANDA-I and the Omaha system, in their own practice, and systematically combine this with information gathered during their work. Students will learn how to assess a care recipient’s self-management. They will also explore each phase of the nursing process through self-study, teaching sessions and workplace learning, during which they will learn to make the right choices and implement them in practice.
Students develop the basic communication skills required to build a relationship with the care recipient and gather relevant information through teaching sessions involving simulated conversations, with a focus on person-centred communication and the use of ICT.
During the sessions, students gain insight into their own learning process and the steps they need to take to achieve the learning outcome. This is achieved, amongst other things, by giving and receiving feedback.
Competence Proficiency Level 1 (CBN, 2022)
At the first level, the context is of medium complexity, with the focus on the methodical application of knowledge and skills in accordance with guidelines and protocols in varying but similar situations. The nature of the task is structured, involving the application of familiar methods.
The student learns to manage their own learning (self-direction) in terms of planning, motivation and reflection. Reflection is aimed at knowledge and understanding, with a focus on innovation.
The guidance provided here is aimed at increasing self-direction.
Assessment:
In this course, students’ competences are assessed on the basis of specific learning outcomes, with the indicators serving as a guide and support for the assessment. The assessment consists of a portfolio assessment. Feedback is provided on the individual pieces of evidence for the portfolio. The portfolio assessment is marked using a rubric with a grade and must be passed.
TEST 01 – BVZa – N1 – Nursing Process and Communication
Evidence for the assessment
Orientation to the nursing profession
Individual assignment
Using a format of their own choosing (e.g. vlog, recorded presentation), the student demonstrates that they have explored the development of the nursing profession, the nursing code of practice, the nursing philosophy and relevant legislation and regulations, and what this means for their own development as a nurse.
Feedback from the tutor
The Nursing Process
Individual assignment
The student has fully explained the nursing process to a care recipient at their own work-based learning placement and translated this into a care record using a classification system (e.g. NANDA-I or the Omaha System). In doing so, attention has been paid to how the care recipient’s self-management capabilities can be identified.
In practice, the student collects at least one practice evaluation demonstrating that, within a moderately complex situation and under supervision, the student determines the nursing process for a care recipient based on clinical reasoning, in accordance with the prevailing nursing philosophy.
Practical supervisor’s declaration of authenticity
Lecturer’s feedback
Simulated professional (care) consultation
Individual assignment
A recording of a (simulated) anamnesis consultation or evaluation consultation, together with the student’s self-assessment
Feedback from fellow students and the lecturer on communication skills
In practice, the student collects at least two brief practice evaluations demonstrating that they communicate in a person-centred and professional manner with the care recipient, their relatives and other healthcare professionals within a moderately complex situation, in order to encourage self-management

/en/course/2026/HVMP26SLO1.content:
In skills labeducation, the emphasis is on learning and mastering various nursing techniques from a holistic and person-centred perspective, underpinned by theoretical principles. Students work in accordance with protocols, guidelines and quality standards, and develop the ability to deviate from these, where necessary, in a conscious and reasoned manner, based on the context and the wishes of the care recipient.
This course covers the fundamentals of nursing practice, such as maintaining hygiene, providing basic care and ensuring the comfort, safety and wellbeing of the care recipient. Through e-learning modules, instructional lessons and scenario-based training, students work specifically on their own professional development. Students receive feedback on their attitude, communication and technical skills as part of their training, either in a simulated setting or during workplace learning.

Hygiene
Basic care (ADL, oral care, elimination, compression therapy, repositioning techniques)
Vital signs
Nursing documentation (EPD)
Oral medication, nebuliser therapy and oxygen administration

/en/course/2026/HVMB26BVZB1.content:
Nurses are increasingly being asked to consider what the best course of action is. In addition to their professional expertise, knowledge and the wishes of the patient and their loved ones, knowledge is set out in protocols and guidelines. However, not all current knowledge and insights are set out in guidelines and protocols. It may be necessary for nurses to search the scientific literature themselves to find the answer to the question of what constitutes the ‘best’ care in a given situation.
In this course, students learn skills relating to critical thinking. Using the steps of the EBP methodology, students can underpin nursing care with scientific evidence in order to arrive at a recommendation for the patient and their own professional practice.
Students learn to formulate a clinical question from their own professional practice into a question that can be answered. They then learn to search databases efficiently for relevant scientific sources and to assess these scientific articles methodologically. This enables students, based on that assessment, to formulate an answer to the question and arrive at a recommendation for their own professional practice.
During the sessions, students gain insight into their own learning process and the steps they need to take to achieve the learning outcome. This is achieved, amongst other things, through giving and receiving feedback.

/en/course/2026/HVMB26BVZPLN2.content:
This course consists of two parts: ‘justifying care’ and ‘carrying out restricted and high-risk procedures’.
In ‘justifying care’, the novice practitioner demonstrates that they have mastered all stages of clinical reasoning and that they can integrate and apply theory and practice in a specific nursing situation. In doing so, the novice practitioner involves the care recipient and/or their relatives. During the sessions, themed topics will be used to provide in-depth theoretical knowledge in the area of expertise ‘justifying care’ and to offer opportunities to practise communication skills.
During the sessions, the student gains insight into their own learning process and the steps they need to take to achieve the learning outcome. This is achieved, amongst other things, through giving and receiving feedback.
For the ‘performing restricted and high-risk procedures’ module assessment, the novice practitioner may undertake training at their own workplace, at a certified institute or at the academy. The novice practitioner deepens their theoretical knowledge via e-learning and may enrol for training and assessment on a per-skill basis. During the final-year phase, several training courses are offered, except for BLS/AED. The novice practitioner must arrange this themselves.
Competence Proficiency Level 2 (CBN, 2022)
The second level involves a highly complex context in which the focus is on acting methodically in unpredictable, complex situations. The nature of the task is complex and unstructured. The focus is on student-led learning, with guidance provided on an ad hoc basis. Actions are carried out as independently as possible, with justification provided afterwards. The novice professional is encouraged to apply (strategic) planning, self-efficacy, motivation and reflection independently. Reflection on one’s actions centres on daring, willing and being, with the emphasis on sustainable development.
Assessment:
In this course, students’ competences are assessed on the basis of specific learning outcomes, with the indicators serving as a guide and support for the assessment. Both assessments consist of portfolio assessments, which are marked using a rubric with a grade and must achieve a pass mark.

In this course, the novice practitioner develops the skills needed to ensure continuity of care for their own service user(s). The novice professional learns to apply the nursing role within the healthcare sector, including relevant disciplines and legislation. In doing so, the novice professional works on developing nursing leadership. The novice professional expands their knowledge and skills relating to the coordination of care.
During the sessions, the student gains insight into their own learning process and the steps they must take to achieve the learning outcome. This is achieved, amongst other things, by giving and receiving feedback

/en/course/2026/HVMB26BKIPLN2.outcomes:
Area of Expertise and Learning Outcome(s)
4. Ensuring Quality and Innovation – Level 2
LOL 4.1 – BKI – N2
The novice practitioner independently monitors, measures and screens the quality and safety of a quality aspect within a healthcare organisation at both the micro and meso levels, using the most appropriate models within a complex, authentic context. In doing so, the novice professional proactively participates in quality assurance systems to monitor, safeguard or improve the quality of care, in accordance with applicable legislation, regulations and professional standards.
LOL 4.2 - BKI - N2
The novice practitioner demonstrates independent and enterprising behaviour within a complex, authentic context by actively contributing to sustainable innovation, using healthcare technology where appropriate.
Indicators
Description
4.8 Demonstrates personal, professional and organisational leadership (BN2030).
4.9 Initiates and designs a well-founded implementation plan (BN2030).
4.10 Initiates and designs, based on ‘shared governance’, a well-founded improvement plan in the field of care quality or safety, and actively involves relevant stakeholders (BN2030).
4.11 Takes the initiative to improve the quality of care, applying professional standards in doing so and taking responsibility for their own actions (BN2030).
4.12 Considers clinical, economic, environmental and organisational interests within various healthcare contexts when improving the quality of care (BN2030).
4.13 Demonstrates organisational sensitivity by taking into account the informal structure and objectives, and their own influence on these (BN2030).
4.14 Ensures the sustainability of the innovation (BN2030).
4.15 Makes use of healthcare technology where this is feasible and adds value (BN2030).
/en/course/2026/HVMB26BKIPLN2.content:
In this course, the novice professional develops an interprofessional improvement proposal based on an analysis of a quality aspect within the healthcare organisation. In doing so, the novice professional takes the initiative to implement and embed the intended innovation. During the teaching sessions, this improvement proposal is developed step by step. Attention is paid to quality thinking, ethical issues, legislation and regulations, societal developments and organisational interests. Throughout this process, the novice professional actively involves the relevant stakeholders in the decision-making process.
Following the analysis, the professional works methodically to establish the conditions for the innovation. In doing so, they take into account the diverse interests, objectives and potential resistance of stakeholders, as well as formal and informal structures and professional standards within the healthcare context. The final improvement proposal focuses on a sustainable innovation, preferably utilising healthcare technology. Where possible, the proposal is actually implemented.
A quality-oriented mindset is reflected in the use of quality systems and quality measurement tools, and in the ability to analyse, monitor, evaluate and ensure quality at the micro, meso and macro levels. In addition, attention is paid to the entrepreneurial attitude of both novice practitioners and nurses in general, as well as to patient safety. In many situations, healthcare technology can make a valuable contribution in this regard.
Competence Proficiency Level 2 (CBN, 2022)
The second level involves a highly complex context in which the focus is on acting methodically in unpredictable, complex situations. The nature of the task is complex and unstructured. The focus is on student-led learning, with supervision provided more on an on-demand basis. Actions are carried out as independently as possible, with justification provided retrospectively. Novice practitioners are encouraged to apply (strategic) planning, self-efficacy, motivation and reflection independently. Reflection on their actions centres on daring, willing and being, with the focus on sustainable development.
Assessment:
In this course, students’ competences are assessed on the basis of specific learning outcomes, with the indicators serving as a guide and support for the assessment. The assessment consists of a portfolio assessment. The early-career professional determines, in consultation with the lecturer and work supervisor, which supporting documents will be used to demonstrate the learning outcomes. The portfolio assessment is marked using a rubric with a grade and must be passed.

Improvement proposal
The student draws up a proposal for improving a quality aspect of professional practice and submits the following as supporting evidence:
An improvement proposal containing an implementation plan.
A recorded presentation of the improvement proposal in a professional practice setting.

Individual product
Short practical evaluations by relevant parties regarding performance in relation to the learning outcomes associated with the module, which are independent of the learning pathway.
In practice, the student must collect at least one practical evaluation demonstrating that they proactively participate in quality assurance systems within a highly complex situation to monitor, safeguard or improve the quality of care.
In practice, the student must collect at least one practical evaluation demonstrating that they actively contribute to sustainable innovation within a highly complex situation, using healthcare technology where appropriate.
